sections.heading: Newton's Law of Gravitation, Field Intensity & Superposition
sections.summary: Every pair of point masses attracts along the line joining them with magnitude F = G m1 m2 / r^2, establishing a conservative central force field g(r). Superposition lets us build continuous fields for rods, rings, and arcs exactly like electrostatics with k replaced by G and q replaced by -M.
keyPoints: Vector force & universal constant: F_12 = -(G m1 m2 / r^2) r_hat_12, where G = 6.67 x 10^(-11) N m^2 / kg^2 (measured by Cavendish torsion balance; independent of medium!).
Gravitational field intensity g = F / m = -grad(V) points radially inward toward attracting mass; SI unit N/kg = m/s^2.
Null point between two masses M1 and M2 separated by d: Zero net field occurs between them at distance x = d / (1 + sqrt(M2 / M1)) from M1 (closer to the lighter mass!).

Uniform circular ring (M, R) on axis at distance x: g_axis = G M x / (R^2 + x^2)^(3/2). Field is zero at centre (x=0) and infinity, peaking at x = +/- R / sqrt(2) with g_max = 2 G M / (3 sqrt(3) R^2).
Uniform thin rod (M, L): At distance d along perpendicular bisector, g = G M / [d sqrt(d^2 + L^2/4)]; along axis at distance a from near end, g = G M / [a(a + L)].

sections.heading: Gauss's Shell Theorem, Solid Sphere Profiles & Tunnel SHM
sections.summary: By spherical symmetry and inverse-square scaling, a uniform hollow shell exerts zero gravitational pull anywhere inside its cavity while behaving like a point mass at its centre outside. Integrating shell layers builds the linear internal field of a uniform solid sphere and explains Earth-tunnel SHM.
keyPoints: Uniform spherical shell (M, R): For r < R, g_in = 0 and V_in = -GM / R (strictly constant!). At r = R, g jumps discontinuously from 0 to GM / R^2; for r >= R, g = GM / r^2 and V = -GM / r.
Uniform solid sphere (M, R, density rho): For r <= R, g_in = G M r / R^3 = (4/3) pi G rho r (linearly proportional to r!), while V_in = -GM (3 R^2 - r^2) / (2 R^3).
Centre-to-surface potential benchmark for solid sphere: V_centre = -3 G M / (2 R) = 1.5 x V_surface. Maximum |V| occurs at the centre, where g = 0!

Spherical cavity inside uniform solid sphere (centre-to-cavity offset vector d): By superposition of +rho sphere and -rho cavity, field inside the cavity is UNIFORM: g_cavity = (4/3) pi G rho d (parallel to vector from sphere centre to cavity centre!).

Tunnel through uniform Earth (along diameter OR any straight chord!): Restoring force along tunnel is F_parallel = -m g_in cos(theta) = -(G M m / R^3) x, producing SHM with period T = 2 pi sqrt(R^3 / GM) = 2 pi sqrt(R / g) ~ 84.6 minutes, completely independent of chord orientation!

sections.heading: Variation of Acceleration Due to Gravity g (Altitude, Depth, Rotation)
sections.summary: Surface gravity g_0 = GM / R^2 ~ 9.8 m/s^2 decreases both above Earth's surface (inverse-square) and below it (linear drop inside uniform Earth), as well as toward the equator due to Earth's axial rotation. Using the small-height binomial approximation for large altitudes is a classic exam pitfall.
keyPoints: Altitude h above surface: Exact formula g(h) = g_0 / (1 + h/R)^2 = g_0 R^2 / (R + h)^2. ONLY when h << R may you approximate g(h) ~ g_0 (1 - 2 h / R).

Depth d below surface (uniform Earth): g(d) = g_0 (1 - d / R) exact for all 0 <= d <= R, dropping linearly to 0 at Earth's centre (r = 0). For small h << R, equal fractional drop in g occurs when depth d = 2 h.

Earth rotation at latitude lambda (equator lambda = 0, poles lambda = 90 deg): Apparent gravity g' = sqrt(g^2 - 2 g omega^2 R cos^2 lambda + omega^4 R^2 cos^2 lambda) ~ g - omega^2 R cos^2(lambda). Poles unaffected (g' = g); equator reduced most (g' = g - omega^2 R).
Weightlessness angular speed: Objects at equator would feel weightless if Earth spun at omega_crit = sqrt(g / R) ~ 17 times current spin rate (day length ~ 84.6 min!).
Shape oblateness effect: Earth's equatorial radius exceeds polar radius by ~21 km, contributing an additional ~0.018 m/s^2 reduction at the equator (total g_pole - g_eq ~ 0.052 m/s^2).

sections.heading: Gravitational Potential Energy, Lifting Work & Escape Velocity
sections.summary: Choosing zero potential energy at infinite separation sets U(r) = -GMm/r negative for all bound configurations. Escape velocity v_e = sqrt(2GM/R) represents the exact kinetic threshold needed to lift total mechanical energy E = K + U to zero at infinity.
keyPoints: Potential energy & lifting work: U(r) = -G M m / r. Exact work to raise mass m from surface (R) to height h: W = Delta U = m g h / (1 + h / R). Note: At h = R, W = m g R / 2 (NOT m g R!); at h -> infinity, W = m g R.
Three-particle system self/interaction energy: U_sys = -G [m1 m2/r12 + m2 m3/r23 + m1 m3/r13]. Self-energy of uniform solid sphere = -3 G M^2 / (5 R); hollow shell = -G M^2 / (2 R).
Escape velocity from surface: (1/2) m v_e^2 - G M m / R = 0 => v_e = sqrt(2 G M / R) = sqrt(2 g R) ~ 11.2 km/s for Earth. Strictly independent of projectile mass m and launch angle!
Hyperbolic excess speed: If launched from surface at v > v_e, residual speed at infinity is v_inf = sqrt(v^2 - v_e^2) (NEVER v - v_e!).
Maximum height reached when launched at v < v_e: (1/2) m v^2 - GMm/R = -GMm/(R + h) => h = R v^2 / (v_e^2 - v^2). For v = v_e / sqrt(2), h = R.
Black hole Schwarzschild radius: Setting v_e = c yields R_s = 2 G M / c^2.

sections.heading: Orbital Satellite Mechanics, Binding Energy & Binary Stars
sections.summary: A circular satellite of radius r balances gravity with centripetal force, locking its kinetic, potential, and total energies in an exact -1 : 2 : 1 magnitude ratio. In binary star systems, both stars revolve around their stationary Centre of Mass with identical angular frequency.
keyPoints: Circular orbit at radius r = R + h: Orbital speed v_o = sqrt(G M / r) = R sqrt(g / r). Near Earth surface (r ~ R): v_o = sqrt(g R) = v_e / sqrt(2) ~ 7.92 km/s; T_min = 2 pi sqrt(R / g) ~ 84.6 min.
Energy virial ratios (circular orbit): K = +G M m / (2 r); U = -G M m / r; Total E = K + U = -G M m / (2 r) = -K = U / 2. Negative E signifies a bound orbit; Binding Energy BE = |E| = +G M m / (2 r).

Atmospheric drag paradox: Slight air drag lowers total energy E (more negative), shrinking orbital radius r, which INCREASES kinetic energy K and orbital speed v_o while decreasing potential energy U twice as fast!
Geostationary vs Polar satellites: Geostationary stays over equator (inclination 0 deg), W-to-E sense, T = 24 h (h ~ 35,800 km, r ~ 6.6 R_E). Polar satellites orbit N-S at ~500-800 km altitude.

Binary stars (masses m1, m2 separated by d): Both orbit common COM at radii r1 = m2 d / (m1 + m2) and r2 = m1 d / (m1 + m2) with equal omega: G m1 m2 / d^2 = m1 omega^2 r1 => T = 2 pi sqrt(d^3 / [G (m1 + m2)]).

sections.heading: Kepler's Three Laws & Elliptical Orbit Conservation
sections.summary: Kepler's laws express central-force geometry, angular momentum conservation, and inverse-square energy scaling for elliptical planetary orbits. Conserving both L and E between perigee and apogee resolves speeds and turning distances in any bound ellipse.
keyPoints: Kepler 1st Law (Orbits): Planets move in ellipses with the Sun at one focus. Semi-major axis a = (r_min + r_max)/2; eccentricity e = (r_max - r_min) / (r_max + r_min); r_min = a(1 - e), r_max = a(1 + e).
Kepler 2nd Law (Areas): Radius vector sweeps equal areas in equal times: dA/dt = L / (2 m) = constant, which is a direct consequence of zero central torque (L conserved!).
Kepler 3rd Law (Periods): T^2 = [4 pi^2 / (G M)] a^3, so T^2 proportional to a^3 (semi-major axis!). Total energy of ANY elliptical orbit depends ONLY on semi-major axis a: E = -G M m / (2 a).

Perigee vs Apogee speed conservation: By L conservation, v_p r_min = v_a r_max (planet moves fastest at closest approach!). By energy conservation, (1/2) v_p^2 - GM/r_min = (1/2) v_a^2 - GM/r_max = -GM / (2 a).

Orbit classification by launch speed v at distance r_0 (perpendicular to radius): v < v_o -> ellipse (r_0 is apogee); v = v_o -> circle; v_o < v < v_e -> ellipse (r_0 is perigee); v = v_e -> parabola; v > v_e -> hyperbola.

derivationsAndGraphs.keyTakeaway: Maximum gravity occurs strictly on Earth's surface (r = R); any movement up OR down reduces g.

derivationsAndGraphs.keyTakeaway: As r increases, U increases (becomes less negative), E increases (needs positive thruster energy to boost orbit), and K decreases!

derivationsAndGraphs.keyTakeaway: Eliminating v_a gives v_p = sqrt[(GM/a) * (1+e)/(1-e)] and v_a = sqrt[(GM/a) * (1-e)/(1+e)].

solvedExamples.question: Find the height h above Earth's surface (radius R) where acceleration due to gravity drops to 1/9th of its surface value g. At what depth d below the surface is g also g/9?
steps: For altitude h: Use exact inverse-square law g(h) = g / (1 + h/R)^2.
For depth d (assuming uniform Earth): g(d) = g (1 - d/R).
solvedExamples.pitfall: Applying g(1 - 2h/R) = g/9 yields h = 4R/9, completely invalid because h is not << R.

solvedExamples.question: A body is projected vertically upward from Earth's surface with speed v = (1/2) v_e, where v_e is escape velocity. Find the maximum height h reached above the surface in terms of Earth radius R.
steps: Recall v_e^2 = 2 G M / R, so initial speed satisfies v^2 = v_e^2 / 4 = G M / (2 R).
At maximum height h (distance r = R + h from centre), speed vanishes (K_f = 0).
Conserve mechanical energy: (1/2) m v^2 - G M m / R = -G M m / (R + h).
Divide by m and substitute v^2 = GM/(2R): GM/(4R) - GM/R = -GM/(R + h) => -3/(4R) = -1/(R + h).
Solve: R + h = 4 R / 3 => h = R / 3.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Using mgh = (1/2) m v^2 assumes constant g and wrongly yields h = R/4!

solvedExamples.question: A satellite orbits Earth in a circular orbit of radius r with kinetic energy K. How much minimum additional energy must be supplied to shift it to an unbound escape state?
steps: For circular orbit of radius r: K = +G M m / (2 r) and U = -G M m / r.
Total mechanical energy in orbit: E_initial = K + U = -G M m / (2 r) = -K.
To just escape to infinity (E_final = 0), minimum energy needed = E_final - E_initial = 0 - (-K) = +K.
Verify via escape speed: v_e(r) = sqrt(2) v_o(r), so K_escape = 2 K_orbit => additional KE needed = 2K - K = K.
solvedExamples.answer: K (equal to its current orbital kinetic energy)
solvedExamples.pitfall: Answering 2K by confusing potential energy magnitude |U| = 2K with total binding energy |E| = K!

solvedExamples.question: A planet of mass m orbits a star of mass M in an ellipse with perigee distance r_1 = R and apogee distance r_2 = 3 R. Find the ratio of speeds v_1 / v_2, the speed v_1 at perigee, and the time period T.
steps: Conserve angular momentum at perigee and apogee (velocity is perpendicular to radius vector at both): m v_1 r_1 = m v_2 r_2 => v_1 / v_2 = r_2 / r_1 = 3 / 1 = 3.
Semi-major axis of ellipse: a = (r_1 + r_2)/2 = (R + 3R)/2 = 2 R.
Total energy E = -G M m / (2 a) = -G M m / (4 R).
Apply energy at perigee: (1/2) m v_1^2 - G M m / R = -G M m / (4 R) => (1/2) v_1^2 = 3 G M / (4 R) => v_1 = sqrt(3 G M / (2 R)).
Apply Kepler's 3rd Law using a = 2 R: T = 2 pi sqrt(a^3 / (GM)) = 2 pi sqrt(8 R^3 / (GM)) = 4 pi sqrt(2 R^3 / (GM)).
solvedExamples.answer: v1/v2 = 3 ; v1 = sqrt(3GM/(2R)) ; T = 4 pi sqrt(2 R^3 / GM)
solvedExamples.pitfall: Using r_1 or sqrt(r_1 r_2) instead of semi-major axis a = (r_1 + r_2)/2 in Kepler's 3rd Law and total energy!

sections.heading: Elasticity, Stress-Strain Curve, Elastic Energy & Thermal Stress
sections.summary: Solids resist deformation via restoring internal stress proportional to strain within the proportional limit. Combining Young's, Bulk, and Shear moduli with Poisson's ratio and thermal expansion solves composite rods, self-weight sag, and clamped thermal stress.
keyPoints: Moduli definitions: Stress sigma = F_perp/A, Longitudinal strain = dL/L -> Young's Y = F L / (A dL); Bulk modulus B = -Delta P / (Delta V / V) = 1 / Compressibility kappa; Shear modulus G (or eta) = F_tan / (A theta).

Poisson's ratio sigma_P = -(lateral strain dr/r) / (longitudinal strain dL/L): Theoretical range -1 <= sigma_P <= 0.5, actual materials 0 < sigma_P < 0.5. Exact identities: Y = 3 B (1 - 2 sigma_P) = 2 G (1 + sigma_P); 9/Y = 1/B + 3/G.
Self-weight elongation: Uniform rod of mass M, length L, weight W = Mg hanging vertically stretches by dL = W L / (2 A Y) (half the stretch caused by point load W at bottom!).

Elastic potential energy density: u = U / Volume = (1/2) x stress x strain = sigma^2 / (2 Y) = (1/2) Y (strain)^2 (area under stress-strain curve!). Total work in stretching wire = (1/2) F dL (other half lost as heat if load hung suddenly!).

Thermal stress in rigidly clamped rod: Free thermal expansion dL = L alpha Delta T prevented -> compressive strain = alpha Delta T -> thermal stress sigma_th = Y alpha Delta T (independent of rod length L!), Force F = Y A alpha Delta T.

Stress-strain curve landmarks: Proportional limit -> Elastic limit (yield point) -> Ultimate tensile strength (breaking stress depends ONLY on material, NOT cross-section) -> Fracture point. Large plastic zone = ductile; tiny plastic zone = brittle; S-shaped non-linear = elastomer.

sections.heading: Hydrostatics, Buoyancy, Accelerating & Rotating Fluids
sections.summary: In static incompressible fluids, pressure increases linearly with depth perpendicular to the free surface, producing buoyant upthrust equal to displaced fluid weight. Inside accelerating or rotating containers, the free surface aligns perpendicular to the effective gravity vector g_eff.
keyPoints: Hydrostatic pressure & Pascal's Law: P(h) = P_atm + rho g h (independent of container shape — hydrostatic paradox!). Hydraulic lift force F2 = F1 (A2 / A1) conserves work F1 d1 = F2 d2.
Archimedes' Principle: Buoyant force F_B = V_submerged * rho_liquid * g_eff acts upward through Centre of Buoyancy (COM of displaced fluid). Floating fraction V_in / V_total = rho_body / rho_liquid.

Floating ice-melting benchmarks: (a) Pure ice or ice with embedded cork/air bubble floating in pure water -> water level stays UNCHANGED upon melting; (b) Ice with embedded iron/stone sinker -> level DROPS; (c) Pure ice melting in denser brine (rho_liquid > rho_water) -> level RISES!

Linearly accelerating tank (horizontal a_x, vertical a_y): Effective gravity g_eff = sqrt(a_x^2 + (g + a_y)^2); free surface tilts at tan(theta) = a_x / (g + a_y) perpendicular to g_eff. Isobars remain parallel to tilted free surface!
Rotating cylinder (angular velocity omega): Pressure rises radially as P(r) = P_0 + (1/2) rho omega^2 r^2, shaping the free surface into a paraboloid z(r) = omega^2 r^2 / (2 g).

sections.heading: Fluid Dynamics: Continuity, Bernoulli's Theorem & Torricelli Efflux
sections.summary: Steady, incompressible, non-viscous, irrotational streamline flow conserves mass flux (A v = const) and mechanical energy per unit volume along a streamline. Bernoulli's equation explains Venturi pressure drops, Pitot speed tubes, dynamic lift, and Torricelli orifice efflux.
keyPoints: Equation of Continuity: A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2 (incompressible), giving faster speed in narrower constrictions. General compressible form: rho A v = const.
Bernoulli's Energy Equation: P + (1/2) rho v^2 + rho g h = constant along a streamline (note: P = static pressure, (1/2) rho v^2 = dynamic pressure, rho g h = hydrostatic pressure).
Venturimeter flow speed: v_1 = A_2 sqrt( 2 g h_manometer / (A_1^2 - A_2^2) ), or using rho_m in U-tube manometer replace g h by (rho_m / rho - 1) g h.
Torricelli's Theorem (tank area A >> hole area a, hole at depth h below surface, total tank height H): Efflux speed v = sqrt(2 g h); if tank area A is NOT >> a, v = sqrt(2 g h / (1 - a^2/A^2)).

Efflux horizontal range & emptying time: Ground range R = 2 sqrt(h (H - h)), identical for depths h and (H - h), peaking at h = H/2 with R_max = H! Time to lower level from H1 to H2: t = (A / a) sqrt(2/g) * [sqrt(H1) - sqrt(H2)].

Dynamic lift & Magnus effect: Asymmetric airflow over aerofoil or spinning ball creates higher speed -> lower static pressure on one side (Delta P = (1/2) rho (v_top^2 - v_bot^2)), generating net lift force.

sections.heading: Viscosity, Poiseuille Flow, Reynolds Number & Stokes' Terminal Velocity
sections.summary: Fluid viscosity generates internal shear drag proportional to velocity gradient dv/dy, creating parabolic laminar pipe flow and damping falling spheres to a constant terminal velocity. Reynolds number distinguishes smooth streamline flow from dissipative turbulence.
keyPoints: Newton's Law of Viscosity: F = -eta A (dv/dy); SI unit of coefficient of viscosity eta is Pa.s = N.s/m^2 = kg/(m.s); CGS unit is Poise (1 Pa.s = 10 Poise). Viscosity of liquids DECREASES with T, while viscosity of gases INCREASES with sqrt(T)!

Poiseuille's formula (laminar pipe flow, radius r, length L, pressure drop Delta P): Volume flow rate Q = pi Delta P r^4 / (8 eta L). Fluid resistance R_f = 8 eta L / (pi r^4) obeys series/parallel rules just like electrical resistance!
Reynolds Number: N_R = rho v D / eta (dimensionless). Laminar flow for N_R < 1000-2000; turbulent above ~2000.
Stokes' Law (sphere radius r moving at v in infinite viscous medium): Viscous drag F_v = 6 pi eta r v (always proportional to r and v!).

Terminal velocity v_T: Balancing downward weight with upward buoyancy + Stokes drag gives v_T = 2 r^2 (rho_sphere - rho_fluid) g / (9 eta) proportional to r^2! If fluid is denser than sphere (air bubble in water), v_T is negative (rises upward!).

sections.heading: Surface Tension, Surface Energy & Excess Pressure in Drops/Bubbles
sections.summary: Cohesive molecular imbalances at a liquid interface produce surface tension S (force per unit length = surface energy per unit surface area). Curved menisci sustain higher pressure on their concave side to balance surface tension, driving drop coalescence energy release and bubble equilibrium.
keyPoints: Surface Tension S = F / L = Delta U / Delta A (units N/m = J/m^2). Decreases with rising temperature (vanishes at critical temperature T_c) and with soluble impurities like soap/detergent (increases slightly with highly soluble salts like NaCl).

Number of free liquid-air interfaces: Liquid drop in air or air bubble inside water has 1 interface (Delta A = 4 pi R^2). Soap bubble in air or soap film on wire frame has 2 interfaces (multiply area by 2 -> Delta A = 8 pi R^2)!

Excess pressure (always higher on CONCAVE side): Liquid drop / air bubble in liquid: Delta P = 2 S / R; Soap bubble in air: Delta P = 4 S / R; General double-radii surface: Delta P = S (1/R1 + 1/R2); Liquid film trapped between two parallel plates at gap d: Delta P = 2 S cos(theta) / d -> attraction force F = 2 S A cos(theta) / d!

Coalescing n identical droplets (radius r) into 1 big drop (R = n^(1/3) r): Volume conserved -> U_final / U_initial = n^(-1/3) < 1, so energy Delta U = 4 pi R^3 S (1/r - 1/R) is RELEASED! Temperature rise Delta T = 3 S / (rho J c) * (1/r - 1/R).
Splitting 1 big drop into n identical droplets absorbs energy Delta U = 4 pi R^2 S (n^(1/3) - 1) and COOLS the liquid!
Connected bubbles paradox: Connecting a smaller bubble (r1) and larger bubble (r2) via a tube causes air to flow from SMALLER (higher 4S/r1) to LARGER bubble until smaller shrinks away!

sections.heading: Angle of Contact, Wetting & Jurin's Capillary Rise
sections.summary: The balance of adhesive (liquid-solid) and cohesive (liquid-liquid) forces fixes the contact angle theta, curving the meniscus inside narrow tubes. Jurin's Law h = 2 S cos(theta) / (r rho g) relates capillary ascent or depression to meniscus radius and tube geometry.
keyPoints: Angle of contact theta (measured inside the liquid between solid wall and tangent to meniscus): Acute (theta < 90 deg, concave meniscus, adhesive > cohesive, wets glass -> e.g. water-glass ~ 0-8 deg); Obtuse (theta > 90 deg, convex meniscus, cohesive > adhesive, does NOT wet -> e.g. mercury-glass ~ 135-140 deg).
Jurin's Capillary Rise Law: Meniscus radius R_m = r / cos(theta). Equating 2 S / R_m = rho g h yields h = 2 S cos(theta) / (r rho g). Notice h * r = constant for same liquid-tube pair!
Tilted capillary tube (angle alpha to vertical): Vertical height h remains strictly unchanged, while length of liquid column along tube stretches to l = h / cos(alpha).
Tube of insufficient vertical length h' < h: Liquid NEVER overflows as a fountain! Instead, it rises to the rim and flattens its meniscus radius R'_m such that h' R'_m = h R_m = 2 S / (rho g)!
Free fall / Lift / Space station: When g_eff = 0, capillary water rises smoothly to the FULL available length of the tube without overflowing.

derivationsAndGraphs.keyTakeaway: Toughness equals total area up to fracture; resilience equals area up to elastic limit; steeper initial slope means stiffer Young's modulus Y.

derivationsAndGraphs.keyTakeaway: Because v_T proportional to r^2, coalescing 8 identical raindrops (radius doubles to 2r) quadruples terminal speed to 4 v_T!

Melting ice in brine (salt water denser than fresh water): Ice displaces less volume of dense brine than the fresh meltwater volume it produces, so the level RISES!

Sudden vs gradual load on elastic wire: Sudden hanging of mass M stretches wire transiently to TWICE the static extension (2 Mg L / AY) before settling to Mg L / AY (50% energy lost as oscillations/heat!).
Capillary tube tilted at angle alpha: Vertical height h stays constant, NOT the slanted length of water column!

solvedExamples.question: Two identical copper wires of length L and cross-section A are joined (a) in series and (b) in parallel, and subjected to the same total tensile force F. Find the ratio of total elongation and total stored elastic energy in (series : parallel).
steps: Single wire stiffness k = Y A / L; elongation under F is e_0 = F / k.
In series (length 2L, force F in both): k_series = k / 2 => e_series = F / (k/2) = 2 e_0.
In parallel (area 2A, force F/2 in each): k_parallel = 2 k => e_parallel = F / (2k) = e_0 / 2.
Elongation ratio e_series / e_parallel = 2 e_0 / (e_0 / 2) = 4 : 1.
Since U = (1/2) F e under equal load F, energy ratio U_series / U_parallel = e_series / e_parallel = 4 : 1.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Using U = (1/2) k e^2 with fixed e instead of fixed F reverses the energy ratio!

solvedExamples.question: Eight identical spherical water drops of radius r = 1 mm fall through air at terminal velocity v_1 = 2 cm/s. If they coalesce into one single big spherical drop, find its new terminal velocity v_2.
steps: Volume conservation: (4/3) pi R^3 = 8 x (4/3) pi r^3 => R = 8^(1/3) r = 2 r.
Stokes' terminal velocity scales as square of radius: v_T = [2 (rho - sigma) g / (9 eta)] * r^2 proportional to r^2.
Compute ratio: v_2 / v_1 = (R / r)^2 = 2^2 = 4.
Hence v_2 = 4 x 2 cm/s = 8 cm/s.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Scaling v_T linearly with R (giving 4 cm/s) or with volume R^3 (giving 16 cm/s).

solvedExamples.question: Water rises to a height of 10 cm in a capillary tube of radius r. If the same tube is dipped in water so that only 6 cm extends above the water surface, what happens, and what is the new radius of curvature of the meniscus?
steps: Since available length h' = 6 cm < Jurin height h = 10 cm, water rises up to the top rim (6 cm) and stops WITHOUT overflowing.
For water-glass, contact angle theta ~ 0 deg, so initial meniscus radius R_m = r / cos(0) = r.
Equilibrium constant relation: h * R_m = 2 S / (rho g) = h' * R'_m.
Substitute: 10 x r = 6 x R'_m => R'_m = (10 / 6) r = (5 / 3) r (meniscus flattens!).
solvedExamples.answer: No overflow; meniscus flattens to radius (5/3) r
solvedExamples.pitfall: Claiming water overflows continuously like a fountain (violates conservation of energy!).

solvedExamples.question: Two soap bubbles of radii r_1 = 3 cm and r_2 = 4 cm coalesce isothermally in vacuum (external pressure = 0) to form a single soap bubble of radius R. Find R. What if they coalesce isothermally in air at atmospheric pressure P_0?
steps: In vacuum (P_ext = 0): Excess pressure P_i = 4 S / r_i, volume V_i = (4/3) pi r_i^3. Isothermal mole conservation: P_1 V_1 + P_2 V_2 = P V.
With r_1 = 3, r_2 = 4: R = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = 5 cm (surface area conserved strictly in vacuum!).
Notice in air, 3 P_0 Delta V + 4 S Delta A = 0, so R lies between (r_1^3 + r_2^3)^(1/3) ~ 4.50 cm and sqrt(r_1^2 + r_2^2) = 5 cm!
solvedExamples.answer: In vacuum: R = 5 cm ; In air P_0: P_0(r1^3 + r2^3 - R^3) + 4S(r1^2 + r2^2 - R^2) = 0
solvedExamples.pitfall: Using volume conservation r_1^3 + r_2^3 = R^3 in vacuum, or using r_1^2 + r_2^2 = R^2 when ambient P_0 != 0!

sections.heading: Thermal Expansion, Pendulum Clocks & Calorimetry
sections.summary: Raising temperature shifts asymmetric interatomic potentials outward, expanding lengths, areas, and volumes proportionally unless constrained. Calorimetry balances sensible heat m c Delta T and latent phase change m L inside insulated vessels.
keyPoints: Isotropic expansion: Linear dL = L alpha dT; Areal beta = 2 alpha; Volumetric gamma = 3 alpha. Anisotropic crystals: gamma = alpha_x + alpha_y + alpha_z.
Cavity / Hole expansion: Heating a solid metal plate with a circular hole EXPANDS the hole at the EXACT same rate as a solid disc of that metal (photographic enlargement!).

Apparent liquid expansion in container: Delta V_app = V_0 (gamma_liquid - gamma_container) Delta T. Liquid level rises if gamma_l > 3 alpha_vessel; drops if gamma_l < 3 alpha_vessel. Water shows anomalous contraction from 0 C to 4 C (max density at 4 C).

Pendulum clock thermal error: T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g) => fractional time error Delta T / T = (1/2) alpha Delta theta. In summer (hotter), L increases -> T increases -> clock runs SLOW (loses seconds/day = 43200 alpha Delta theta).

Buoyancy & scale reading with T: True length using expanded metal scale (calibrated at T_0, used at T > T_0): L_true = L_read [1 + alpha_scale (T - T_0)]. Floating body submergence changes according to (gamma_liquid - gamma_solid).

Calorimetry & Water Equivalent: W_eq = m_cal * c_cal / c_water (mass of water absorbing same heat per deg C). For ice-steam mixing, always check max heat available from cooling hot component to 0 C (or 100 C) before assuming complete phase change!

sections.heading: Heat Conduction, Thermal Ohm's Law & Pond Ice Growth
sections.summary: Steady-state conduction transfers thermal energy via lattice vibrations and free electrons at a rate governed by Fourier's Law, mathematically identical to DC Ohm's Law. Non-steady phase growth such as lake freezing integrates latent heat conduction over growing ice thickness.
keyPoints: Fourier's Law (steady state): H = dQ/dt = -k A (dT/dx) = (T_1 - T_2) / R_th, where Thermal Resistance R_th = L / (k A). Across a steady uniform rod, temperature gradient dT/dx is constant (linear T vs x).
Composite slab analogies: Series (same heat current H): R_eq = R1 + R2 -> k_eq = (L1 + L2) / (L1/k1 + L2/k2); Parallel (same Delta T): 1/R_eq = 1/R1 + 1/R2 -> k_eq = (k1 A1 + k2 A2) / (A1 + A2).
Radial steady conduction: Cylindrical shell (inner r1, outer r2, length L): R_cyl = ln(r2/r1) / (2 pi k L). Spherical shell (inner r1, outer r2): R_sph = (r2 - r1) / (4 pi k r1 r2).
Wiedemann-Franz intuition: Good electrical conductors (Ag, Cu) carry free electrons and are also top thermal conductors.

Ice formation on pond (air at -T_0 < 0 C, water at 0 C): Heat escaping through thickness x in time dt freezes dx: rho L_f A dx = (k A T_0 / x) dt => time to grow from 0 to x is t = (rho L_f / (2 k T_0)) x^2! Hence 0->1 cm takes 1 hr, 1->2 cm takes 3 hr, 2->3 cm takes 5 hr (odd ratio 1 : 3 : 5!).

sections.heading: Thermal Radiation: Kirchhoff's, Wien's & Stefan-Boltzmann Laws
sections.summary: Every body above absolute zero emits electromagnetic radiation across a continuous spectrum whose peak shifts inversely with Kelvin temperature and whose total power scales with T^4. Kirchhoff's Law links emission and absorption capacities identically at every wavelength.
keyPoints: Interaction partition: a + r + t = 1 (absorptance + reflectance + transmittance). Ideal blackbody: a = 1, r = 0, t = 0 (absorbs all incident wavelengths; appears black at room T yet radiates brightest when white-hot!).

Kirchhoff's Law: At any temperature T and wavelength lambda, e_lambda / a_lambda = E_lambda (blackbody emissive power). Good absorbers are good emitters (rough blackened metal cools faster than polished mirror-finish metal!).
Wien's Displacement Law: lambda_max * T = b = 2.898 x 10^(-3) m.K (peak emission wavelength). Blue star (short lambda) is much hotter than red star (long lambda)!

Stefan-Boltzmann Law: Emitted power P_emit = e sigma A T^4, where sigma = 5.67 x 10^(-8) W/(m^2 K^4) and e = emissivity (0 <= e <= 1). Net power lost in enclosure at T_0: P_net = e sigma A (T^4 - T_0^4).

Rate of cooling comparison (-dT/dt): -dT/dt = [e sigma A / (m c)] (T^4 - T_0^4). Comparing solid vs hollow sphere of SAME outer radius R and material: both radiate equal power P (same A), yet hollow has smaller mass m -> hollow cools FASTER! At same mass m, hollow has larger radius R -> hollow still cools FASTER!
Solar constant & planetary equilibrium temperature: Balancing intercepted solar flux S (pi R_p^2) = 4 pi R_p^2 sigma T_p^4 yields T_p proportional to 1 / sqrt(distance from Sun).

sections.heading: Kinetic Theory of Gases (KTG), Speeds & Equipartition of Energy
sections.summary: Kinetic theory derives macroscopic gas pressure and temperature directly from elastic molecular collisions inside a container. The Equipartition Theorem assigns (1/2) k_B T per quadratic degree of freedom, fixing C_v, C_p, and adiabatic index gamma across atomicity classes.
keyPoints: Ideal gas pressure equation: P = (1/3) (N m / V) v_rms^2 = (1/3) rho v_rms^2, so translational KE per mole = (3/2) R T and per molecule = (3/2) k_B T (depends ONLY on Kelvin temperature T!).
Maxwell speed hierarchy: v_rms = sqrt(3RT/M) > v_avg = sqrt(8RT / (pi M)) > v_mp = sqrt(2RT/M). Ratio v_rms : v_avg : v_mp = 1.732 : 1.596 : 1.414 = sqrt(3) : sqrt(8/pi) : sqrt(2).
Mean free path: lambda_mfp = 1 / (sqrt(2) pi n d^2) = k_B T / (sqrt(2) pi P d^2), where n = N/V is number density and d is molecular diameter.

Degrees of freedom f & Mayer's Law: Monoatomic (He, Ar): f = 3 (C_v = 3R/2, C_p = 5R/2, gamma = 5/3 = 1.67); Diatomic / Linear rigid at room T (N2, O2, CO): f = 5 (C_v = 5R/2, C_p = 7R/2, gamma = 7/5 = 1.40; at high T vibration adds +2 -> f = 7, gamma = 9/7); Non-linear polyatomic rigid (H2O, CH4, NH3): f = 6 (C_v = 3R, C_p = 4R, gamma = 4/3 = 1.33).

Gas mixture formulas (n1, n2 moles): M_mix = (n1 M1 + n2 M2)/(n1 + n2); C_v,mix = (n1 C_v1 + n2 C_v2)/(n1 + n2); C_p,mix = C_v,mix + R; gamma_mix = C_p,mix / C_v,mix (OR use n_total / (gamma_mix - 1) = n1/(gamma1 - 1) + n2/(gamma2 - 1)).

sections.heading: First Law of Thermodynamics & Standard Ideal Gas Processes
sections.summary: The First Law dQ = dU + dW states energy conservation using the Physics work sign convention (dW = +P dV for expansion). For any ideal gas, internal energy change dU = n C_v dT is strictly a state function independent of the thermodynamic path.
keyPoints: Physics Sign Convention: +Q = heat absorbed BY gas; +W = work done BY gas (expansion, dV > 0); +dU = rise in internal energy (rise in T). Warning: Chemistry flips sign of W!
Universal state property: dU = n C_v dT holds for ALL ideal gas processes — reversible, irreversible, free expansion, or cyclic!
Isochoric (V = const): dW = 0, Q = dU = n C_v Delta T, vertical line on P-V graph. Isobaric (P = const): W = P Delta V = n R Delta T, Q = n C_p Delta T, efficiency W/Q = 1 - 1/gamma = R / C_p.
Isothermal (T = const, P V = const): dU = 0, Q = W = n R T ln(V2 / V1) = n R T ln(P1 / P2). Bulk modulus B_iso = P.
Adiabatic (Q = 0, P V^gamma = const, T V^(gamma-1) = const, T^gamma P^(1-gamma) = const): W = -dU = n R (T1 - T2) / (gamma - 1) = (P1 V1 - P2 V2) / (gamma - 1). Bulk modulus B_adia = gamma P.
Free expansion in vacuum (insulated): Q = 0, W = 0 => dU = 0 => T_final = T_initial for ideal gas (irreversible! Cannot apply P V^gamma = const!).

sections.heading: Polytropic Processes, Indicator Diagrams & Cyclic Processes
sections.summary: Generalizing P V^x = constant unifies every standard gas process through a single molar heat capacity formula C = C_v + R / (1 - x). Translating cycles between P-V, V-T, and P-T planes enables rapid computation of net work and cyclic efficiency.
keyPoints: Polytropic molar heat capacity (P V^x = const): C = C_v + R / (1 - x) = R / (gamma - 1) + R / (1 - x). Check limits: x = 0 (isobaric -> C_p), x = 1 (isothermal -> inf), x = gamma (adiabatic -> 0), x -> inf (isochoric -> C_v).

Negative molar heat capacity: Occurs when 1 < x < gamma (e.g., P V^(1.2) = const for air with gamma = 1.4 gives C < 0), meaning gas cools down even while absorbing heat or heats up while rejecting heat!

Slope comparison on P-V diagram: (dP/dV)_adia = -gamma (P/V) = gamma * (dP/dV)_iso. Since gamma > 1, adiabatic curve is STEEPER than isothermal curve at every intersection! Thus adiabatic expansion drops final pressure LOWER and does LESS work than isothermal expansion from same (P_0, V_0) to V_2.
Spring-piston / coupled cylinder work: Work done BY gas = P_0 Delta V + (1/2) k x^2 + m_piston g x (sum of atmosphere + spring + piston PE!).

Cyclic efficiency on closed P-V loop: Delta U_cycle = 0 => Q_net = W_net = enclosed loop area (+ if Clockwise on P-V, - if Counter-Clockwise!). Efficiency eta = W_net / Q_absorbed (divide ONLY by positive Q_in segments, NOT Q_net!).

traps: Celsius vs Kelvin trap: ALWAYS convert C -> K before plugging into PV = nRT, Stefan T^4, Wien lambda*T, or v_rms ~ sqrt(T)! Only Delta T is identical in C and K.
Cavity thermal expansion blunder: Heating a hollow metal shell or perforated washer EXPANDS the inner hole diameter too (never shrinks!).
Adiabatic equation in irreversible processes: P V^gamma = const is valid ONLY for reversible (quasi-static) adiabatic processes — NEVER for sudden free expansion into vacuum!
Cyclic efficiency denominator error: eta = W_net / Q_absorbed divides by POSITIVE heat supplied ONLY, NOT Q_net (= W_net, which always gives 100%!) and NOT Q_in + |Q_out|!
Gas mixture gamma blunder: Mixing 1 mol He (gamma=5/3) and 1 mol N2 (gamma=7/5) gives C_v,mix = 2R => gamma_mix = 1.5, NOT (5/3 + 7/5)/2 = 1.533!
P-V loop orientation: Clockwise loop on P-V gives POSITIVE net work; if V is on y-axis and P is on x-axis, Clockwise gives NEGATIVE net work!

solvedExamples.question: Two identical-dimension rods of thermal conductivities k1 = 200 W/(m.K) and k2 = 400 W/(m.K) are joined in series between reservoirs at 100 C and 0 C. Find the junction temperature T_j and the equivalent conductivity k_eq.
steps: Since length L and area A are equal, thermal resistances satisfy R1 = L/(k1 A) and R2 = L/(k2 A) => R1 / R2 = k2 / k1 = 2 / 1.
In steady series flow, heat current H is equal: (100 - T_j) / R1 = (T_j - 0) / R2.
Notice T_j is closer to the better conductor (0 C side)! For k_eq: 2L / k_eq = L/k1 + L/k2 => k_eq = 2 k1 k2 / (k1 + k2) = 2(200)(400)/600 = 266.7 W/(m.K).
solvedExamples.pitfall: Taking arithmetic mean (200+400)/2 = 300 W/(m.K) (which applies to PARALLEL rods, not series!) or expecting T_j = 50 C.

solvedExamples.question: Two moles of an ideal monoatomic gas undergo a process P = alpha / T (where alpha is a positive constant). Find the molar heat capacity C of the gas during this process.
steps: Use ideal gas law P V = n R T to eliminate T: T = P V / (n R).
Substitute into P = alpha / T => P^2 V = n R alpha = constant => P V^(1/2) = constant.
This is a polytropic process P V^x = constant with polytropic exponent x = 1/2.
For monoatomic gas, C_v = (3/2) R. Apply polytropic formula: C = C_v + R / (1 - x) = (3/2) R + R / (1 - 1/2) = 1.5 R + 2 R = 3.5 R = (7/2) R.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Reading P T = const directly as P V^1 = const (wrong! T depends on BOTH P and V!).

solvedExamples.question: Two spherical blackbodies A and B have radii r_A = 1 m and r_B = 2 m, and temperatures T_A = 4000 K and T_B = 2000 K respectively. Find the ratio of (a) their peak emission wavelengths lambda_A / lambda_B and (b) total radiated powers P_A / P_B.
steps: Apply Wien's Displacement Law: lambda_max * T = b => lambda_A / lambda_B = T_B / T_A = 2000 / 4000 = 1 / 2.
Apply Stefan-Boltzmann Law (e = 1 for blackbodies): P = sigma (4 pi r^2) T^4 proportional to r^2 T^4.
Compute power ratio: P_A / P_B = (r_A / r_B)^2 * (T_A / T_B)^4 = (1 / 2)^2 * (4000 / 2000)^4.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Forgetting the surface area r^2 factor (4 pi r^2) or squaring T instead of raising T to the 4th power.

solvedExamples.question: One mole of an ideal monoatomic gas is taken through a cyclic process A -> B -> C -> A: A(P_0, V_0) -> B(3 P_0, V_0) [isochoric], B -> C(3 P_0, 2 V_0) [isobaric], and C -> A [straight line on P-V]. Find the thermal efficiency of the cycle.
steps: Compute net work = area of right triangle ABC on P-V (Clockwise!): W_net = (1/2) x (2 V_0 - V_0) x (3 P_0 - P_0) = (1/2) V_0 (2 P_0) = P_0 V_0.
Find temperatures (n = 1): T_A = P_0 V_0 / R; T_B = 3 P_0 V_0 / R; T_C = 6 P_0 V_0 / R.
Heat along A -> B (isochoric heating, T rises): Q_AB = C_v (T_B - T_A) = (3/2) R * (2 P_0 V_0 / R) = +3 P_0 V_0 (absorbed!).
Heat along B -> C (isobaric expansion, T rises): Q_BC = C_p (T_C - T_B) = (5/2) R * (3 P_0 V_0 / R) = +7.5 P_0 V_0 (absorbed!).
Check C -> A: Both P and V decrease, so W_CA < 0 and dU_CA < 0 => Q_CA < 0 (heat rejected!). Thus Q_in = Q_AB + Q_BC = 10.5 P_0 V_0, giving eta = W_net / Q_in = 1 / 10.5 = 2 / 21 ~ 9.52%.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Including negative heat Q_CA in the denominator! Always verify sign of dQ along slant lines (sometimes dQ can change sign mid-segment if tangent hits an adiabatic!).

sections.heading: Simple Harmonic Motion (SHM): Kinematics, Phasors & Graphs
sections.summary: SHM occurs whenever restoring acceleration scales linearly opposite to displacement from stable equilibrium: d^2x/dt^2 = -omega^2 x. Mapping SHM onto uniform circular motion (phasor diagram) turns tricky non-uniform travel-time problems into elementary angular geometry.
keyPoints: Standard SHM kinematics: x = A sin(omega t + phi); v = omega A cos(omega t + phi) = +/- omega sqrt(A^2 - x^2); a = -omega^2 x. Phase difference: v leads x by pi/2; a leads v by pi/2 (anti-phase pi with x).
Extreme benchmarks: At mean position (x = 0): v_max = omega A, a = 0. At extreme (x = +/- A): v = 0, a_max = omega^2 A.
Phasor travel-time shortcuts (from mean x = 0): 0 -> A/2 sweeps 30 deg = T/12; A/2 -> A sweeps 60 deg = T/6 (twice as long!); 0 -> A/sqrt(2) sweeps 45 deg = T/8; 0 -> sqrt(3)A/2 sweeps 60 deg = T/6.
Canonical SHM phase graphs: v vs x is an ELLIPSE (v^2/(omega A)^2 + x^2/A^2 = 1); a vs x is a straight line of negative slope -omega^2 through origin.

Superposition of collinear SHMs (same omega): x1 = A1 sin(omega t), x2 = A2 sin(omega t + delta) -> Resultant amplitude A_res = sqrt(A1^2 + A2^2 + 2 A1 A2 cos delta). Perpendicular SHMs (phase pi/2, equal A) trace a circle; general delta gives an ellipse!

sections.heading: Energy Partition, Spring Combinations & Pendulums
sections.summary: In undamped SHM, mechanical energy oscillates cleanly between kinetic and elastic potential forms at twice the mechanical frequency. Equivalent spring rules, cut springs, two-body reduced mass, and physical pendulums follow directly from restoring torque or force constants.
keyPoints: SHM Energy partition: U(x) = (1/2) m omega^2 x^2; K(x) = (1/2) m omega^2 (A^2 - x^2); Total E = (1/2) m omega^2 A^2 = const. K = U = E/2 at x = +/- A / sqrt(2). Time-averaged <K> = <U> = E / 2; K and U oscillate with frequency 2 f!

Spring cutting & combinations: Spring constant k is inversely proportional to length (k * L = const). Cutting a spring in ratio 1 : n gives k1 = (n+1)k and k2 = ((n+1)/n)k. Parallel springs: k_eq = k1 + k2; Series springs: 1/k_eq = 1/k1 + 1/k2.

Two-body spring oscillation (m1, m2 attached to spring k on smooth floor): Both oscillate in opposite phase at T = 2 pi sqrt(mu / k), where reduced mass mu = m1 m2 / (m1 + m2); amplitudes satisfy m1 A1 = m2 A2.

Simple pendulum (small angles): T = 2 pi sqrt(L / g_eff). In lift accelerating up: g_eff = g + a; free fall: g_eff = 0 (T -> inf); car accelerating horizontally: g_eff = sqrt(g^2 + a^2); uniform charge q in E: g_eff = |g + qE/m|; submerged in fluid: g_eff = g(1 - rho_l/rho_s).
Long pendulum (L comparable to Earth radius R): T = 2 pi sqrt(1 / [g (1/L + 1/R)]). For L -> infinity, T saturates at 2 pi sqrt(R / g) ~ 84.6 min (never exceeds this!).
Physical / Compound pendulum & U-tube: T = 2 pi sqrt(I_pivot / (m g d)) = 2 pi sqrt((k^2/d + d)/g), minimized at d = k; liquid in U-tube of total column L oscillates with T = 2 pi sqrt(L / (2 g)).

sections.heading: Progressive Mechanical Waves, Wave Speeds & Intensity
sections.summary: A progressive wave transports energy and momentum without net transport of medium particles, governed by the 1D wave equation d^2y/dt^2 = v^2 (d^2y/dx^2). String tension and gas thermodynamics dictate wave propagation speeds cleanly.
keyPoints: Travelling wave form: y(x, t) = A sin(omega t - k x + phi) moves along +x at phase velocity v = omega / k = f lambda (same signs of omega t and kx -> moves along -x!).

Wave vs Particle velocity: Particle velocity v_p = dy/dt = -v * (dy/dx) = -v * (slope of y-x snapshot!). Particle acceleration a_p = -omega^2 y; max particle speed = omega A (independent of wave speed v!).
Phase & path difference: Delta phi = (2 pi / lambda) Delta x = (2 pi / T) Delta t.

Transverse wave speed on string: v = sqrt(T / mu), where mu = mass / length = rho * A. Heavy rope hanging vertically under own weight: tension T(y) = mu g y -> v(y) = sqrt(g y) -> pulse climbs length L in time t = 2 sqrt(L / g)!

Longitudinal sound speed (Newton-Laplace): v = sqrt(B_adia / rho) = sqrt(gamma P / rho) = sqrt(gamma R T / M). Independent of pressure P at constant temperature! Increases with T (sqrt T) and humidity (water vapour lowers effective M_mix!).

Wave intensity & power: Average intensity I = 2 pi^2 f^2 A^2 rho v = (1/2) rho v omega^2 A^2 = (Delta P_0)^2 / (2 rho v). Point source isotropic spreading: I proportional to 1/r^2 => A proportional to 1/r; cylindrical line source: I proportional to 1/r => A proportional to 1/sqrt(r).

sections.heading: Wave Superposition, Boundary Reflection & Standing Waves on Strings
sections.summary: When two coherent waves of identical frequency and amplitude travel in opposite directions, their superposition traps energy in stationary spatial nodes and antinodes. Boundary rigidity fixes whether reflected waves undergo a pi phase inversion.
keyPoints: Interference of two coherent waves: I_res = I1 + I2 + 2 sqrt(I1 I2) cos(Delta phi). Constructive (max): Delta phi = 2 n pi, Delta x = n lambda; Destructive (min): Delta phi = (2n - 1) pi, Delta x = (2n - 1) lambda / 2. I_max / I_min = [(sqrt(I1) + sqrt(I2)) / (sqrt(I1) - sqrt(I2))]^2.

Boundary reflection rules: Reflection from RIGID / DENSER boundary inverts phase by pi radians (crest -> trough); reflection from FREE / RARER boundary produces ZERO phase change (crest -> crest). Transmitted wave NEVER changes frequency or phase!
Standing wave equation: y = 2 A sin(k x) cos(omega t) (fixed end x = 0 is a node). Adjacent Node-to-Node = Antinode-to-Antinode = lambda / 2; Node-to-Antinode = lambda / 4.

Energy in standing wave: Zero net energy flux passes across any node; energy oscillates locally between pure elastic/potential (at extreme displacement, v_p = 0) and pure kinetic (at mean flat line, v_p = max).

Stretched string harmonics (fixed both ends, length L): f_n = n v / (2 L) = (n / 2L) sqrt(T / mu) for ALL integers n = 1, 2, 3... Number of loops = n; n-th harmonic = (n - 1)-th overtone. Composite wire junction: frequency f stays SAME across both segments!

sections.heading: Organ Pipes, Sound Pressure Nodes & Beats
sections.summary: Air columns resonate whenever boundary conditions match displacement nodes at closed ends and displacement antinodes just outside open ends. Slightly mismatched frequencies interfere temporally to create periodic loudness beats.
keyPoints: Displacement vs Pressure wave phase: Sound displacement wave s(x,t) and excess pressure wave Delta P(x,t) are 90 deg out of phase! Therefore, a displacement NODE is always a PRESSURE ANTINODE (max pressure swing at closed wall!), and a displacement ANTINODE is a PRESSURE NODE (Delta P = 0 at open mouth!).
Open Organ Pipe (open both ends -> antinodes at both ends): Allowed wavelengths lambda_n = 2 L / n; ALL harmonics present: f_n = n v / (2 L) for n = 1, 2, 3... Fundamental f_1 = v / (2 L).

Closed Organ Pipe (closed at x=0, open at x=L): Allowed wavelengths lambda = 4 L / (2n - 1); ONLY ODD harmonics present: f = (2n - 1) v / (4 L) (1 : 3 : 5 : 7...). Fundamental f_1 = v / (4 L) (one octave lower than equal-length open pipe!). First overtone of closed pipe = 3rd harmonic!
End correction e ~ 0.6 r: Open pipe effective length = L + 2 e; closed pipe effective length = L + e.

Beats phenomenon: Superposition of f1 and f2 (|f1 - f2| <= ~10 Hz) produces amplitude modulation at f_beat = |f1 - f2| (waxing-to-waxing time = 1 / |f1 - f2|). Notice beat frequency is |f1 - f2|, NOT (f1 - f2)/2!
Tuning fork rules: Filing the prongs slightly reduces mass/inertia near tips -> INCREASES frequency; loading prongs with wax increases inertia -> DECREASES frequency.

traps: SHM travel time blunder: Moving from x = 0 to A/2 does NOT take T/8! It takes T/12, whereas A/2 to A takes T/6!
Energy frequency trap: If particle SHM frequency is f, kinetic energy K and potential energy U oscillate at 2 f (twice per cycle), NOT f!
Closed pipe 1st overtone error: Calling the 1st overtone of a closed pipe '2 f_1' is wrong! Even harmonics are absent, so 1st overtone = 3rd harmonic = 3 f_1!
Wave direction sign error: y = A sin(omega t + k x) moves in the -x direction, NOT +x! Direction is +x only when signs of t and x are OPPOSITE.
Sound speed & pressure trap: Doubling gas pressure P at constant temperature T doubles density rho identically, leaving v_sound = sqrt(gamma P / rho) UNCHANGED!
Hanging heavy rope wave time: Tension varies with height y, so pulse does NOT take L / sqrt(gL) = sqrt(L/g); it takes 2 sqrt(L / g)!

Verify spring cutting formula k * L = const and two-body reduced mass period.
Check simple pendulum period modifications in accelerating lift, car, E-field, and fluid, plus L -> infinity Earth-radius limit.
Distinguish wave speed v_w = omega/k from particle speed v_p = -v_w (dy/dx) and max particle speed omega A.
Verify phase shifts upon rigid (pi) vs free (0) boundary reflections.

solvedExamples.question: A spring of force constant k is cut into two pieces of lengths in the ratio 1 : 2. A block of mass m is attached to (a) the shorter piece alone and (b) both pieces connected in parallel. Find the ratio of oscillation time periods T_a : T_b.
steps: Spring constant k_piece is inversely proportional to length L: total length L = L/3 + 2L/3.
Shorter piece (L/3): k1 = 3 k. Longer piece (2L/3): k2 = (3/2) k = 1.5 k.
Verify series check: (3k)(1.5k)/(3k + 1.5k) = 4.5k/4.5 = k (exact!).
Parallel combination: k_b = k1 + k2 = 3k + 1.5k = 4.5 k = 9k / 2.
Ratio T_a / T_b = sqrt(k_b / k_a) = sqrt((9k/2) / (3k)) = sqrt(3 / 2).
solvedExamples.pitfall: Taking k proportional to length (k1 = k/3, k2 = 2k/3) instead of inversely proportional!

solvedExamples.question: A particle executes SHM of amplitude A = 8 cm and time period T = 6 s. Find the minimum time taken to travel from x = +4 cm to x = +4 sqrt(3) cm.
steps: Convert positions into phase angles on phasor x = A sin(theta): sin(theta_1) = 4/8 = 1/2 => theta_1 = 30 deg (pi/6).
At x_2 = 4 sqrt(3): sin(theta_2) = sqrt(3)/2 => theta_2 = 60 deg (pi/3).
Minimum phase swept between these two positions (moving in same direction toward +A) = 60 deg - 30 deg = 30 deg = pi/6 rad.
Time taken t = (Delta theta / 360 deg) * T = (30 / 360) x 6 s = 0.5 s.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Computing t(0 -> 4) = T/12 = 0.5 s and t(0 -> 4 sqrt(3)) = T/6 = 1 s, then forgetting to take their difference, or assuming velocity is uniform!

solvedExamples.question: A closed organ pipe and an open organ pipe of equal length L emit 4 beats per second when both vibrate in their fundamental modes. If the length of the open pipe is halved, what is the new frequency ratio and why can an open pipe produce both even and odd harmonics?
steps: Initially: f_open = v / (2 L) and f_closed = v / (4 L) = f_open / 2.
Given beat frequency f_open - f_closed = 4 Hz => f_open / 2 = 4 Hz => f_closed = 4 Hz and f_open = 8 Hz.
When open pipe length is halved (L' = L / 2): f'_open = v / (2 * L/2) = v / L = 2 f_open = 16 Hz.
New frequency ratio f'_open : f_closed = 16 : 4 = 4 : 1 (and open pipe supports all integer harmonics because BOTH ends are symmetric displacement antinodes, enforcing L = n lambda / 2).
solvedExamples.answer: 4 : 1 (L = n lambda / 2 allows all integers n = 1, 2, 3...)
solvedExamples.pitfall: Confusing fundamental frequencies v/(2L) and v/(4L); closed pipe fundamental is ALWAYS half of open pipe of equal length.

solvedExamples.question: A uniform block of mass m = 2 kg rests on a smooth floor attached to a horizontal spring (k = 200 N/m). A bullet of mass m_b = 0.5 kg moving at 10 m/s hits and embeds in the block along the spring axis. Find the subsequent SHM angular frequency, amplitude, and total mechanical energy after impact.
steps: During instantaneous impact (dt -> 0), spring stays unstretched (zero impulse from spring), so linear momentum is conserved: m_b v_0 = (m + m_b) v_cm.
Compute post-impact speed: v_cm = (0.5 x 10) / (2 + 0.5) = 5 / 2.5 = 2 m/s.
Total oscillating mass M_tot = 2.5 kg => angular frequency omega = sqrt(k / M_tot) = sqrt(200 / 2.5) = sqrt(80) = 4 sqrt(5) rad/s.
At equilibrium x = 0, speed is v_max = v_cm = 2 m/s = omega A => amplitude A = v_cm / omega = 2 / sqrt(80) = 1 / sqrt(20) = sqrt(5) / 10 m ~ 0.224 m.
Total SHM energy = (1/2) M_tot v_cm^2 = 0.5 x 2.5 x 4 = 5 J (while 20 J of bullet's initial 25 J KE was lost as heat during embedding!).
solvedExamples.answer: omega = 4 sqrt(5) rad/s ; A = sqrt(5)/10 m ; E_SHM = 5 J
solvedExamples.pitfall: Equating bullet's initial KE (25 J) directly to (1/2) k A^2! Perfectly inelastic impact dissipates 80% of the initial KE before SHM starts!

sections.heading: Coulomb's Law, Continuous Charge Fields & Three-Charge Equilibrium
sections.summary: Electrostatic force F = k q1 q2 r_hat / r^2 obeys linear superposition identically in vacuum and scaled by 1/K inside infinite homogeneous dielectrics. Integrating elementary dq strips yields exact closed-form fields for rods, rings, discs, and infinite planes.
keyPoints: Coulomb's Law in medium (permittivity eps = K eps_0): Mutual force between two charges drops to F_med = F_vac / K, though direct force between q1 and q2 alone remains k q1 q2 / r^2 (bound polarization charges cause the net reduction!). k = 1/(4 pi eps_0) = 9 x 10^9 N m^2 / C^2.

Equilibrium of 3 collinear charges: Placing free third charge q3 between like charges +Q1, +Q2 -> x = d / (1 + sqrt(Q2/Q1)) from Q1. For ALL 3 charges to stay in equilibrium simultaneously, q3 must be OPPOSITE sign with magnitude q3 = -Q1 Q2 / (sqrt(Q1) + sqrt(Q2))^2 (always unstable!).

Continuous fields: (a) Uniform finite rod (lambda) at perp distance d spanning angles theta_1, theta_2: E_perp = (k lambda / d)(sin theta_1 + sin theta_2), E_parallel = (k lambda / d)(cos theta_2 - cos theta_1); Infinite wire: E = 2 k lambda / d = lambda / (2 pi eps_0 d).

(b) Circular arc (angle alpha, radius R, lambda): E = 2 k lambda sin(alpha/2) / R along angle bisector. (c) Circular ring (Q, R) on axis x: E = k Q x / (R^2 + x^2)^(3/2), peaking at x = +/- R / sqrt(2)!

(d) Uniformly charged disc (sigma, radius R) on axis x: E = (sigma / 2 eps_0) [1 - x / sqrt(R^2 + x^2)]. Limiting case R -> inf (infinite plane non-conducting sheet): E = sigma / (2 eps_0) independent of distance!

sections.heading: Electric Dipole, Field/Potential Maps & Torque-SHM Dynamics
sections.summary: An ideal electric dipole p = q d (pointing from -q to +q) dominates far-field multipole physics with 1/r^3 field and 1/r^2 potential decay. In uniform fields a dipole experiences pure torque without net translation, whereas non-uniform fields pull it toward stronger field regions.
keyPoints: Dipole moment p = q * 2a directed strictly FROM -q TO +q. Axial field (theta = 0): E_axial = 2 k p / r^3 (parallel to p); Equatorial field (theta = 90 deg): E_eq = k p / r^3 (ANTI-PARALLEL to p!).

General far-field (r >> a) at polar angle theta from p: Potential V = k p cos(theta) / r^2 (zero everywhere on equatorial plane!); Field magnitude E = (k p / r^3) sqrt(1 + 3 cos^2 theta), tilted at alpha to radius where tan(alpha) = (1/2) tan(theta).

Uniform field E: Net force F_net = 0; Torque tau = p x E = p E sin(theta); Potential Energy U = -p . E = -p E cos(theta). Stable equilibrium at theta = 0 (U = -pE); Unstable at theta = 180 deg (U = +pE).

Dipole small-angle SHM in uniform E: Restoring torque tau = -p E theta = I alpha => T = 2 pi sqrt(I / (p E)). Work to rotate dipole from theta_1 to theta_2: W = p E (cos theta_1 - cos theta_2) (flipping from stable 0 to 180 requires W = 2 p E!).
Non-uniform field & dipole-dipole force: F = (p . grad) E = p (dE/dr) along field gradient. Two collinear aligned dipoles separated by r attract/repel with F = 6 k p1 p2 / r^4!

sections.heading: Electric Flux & Gauss's Law Symmetry Applications
sections.summary: Gauss's Law equates total outward electric flux through any closed surface strictly to q_enclosed / eps_0, regardless of surface distortion or external charges. Exploiting cube, cylinder, and sphere symmetries bypasses surface integrals completely.
keyPoints: Gauss's Law: Phi = integral(E . dA) = q_enclosed / eps_0. Note carefully: E on the surface is produced by ALL charges (inside + outside), whereas flux Phi depends ONLY on q_enclosed!

Gaussian cube symmetry benchmarks for charge q: (1) At cube centre -> Phi_cube = q/eps_0, per face = q/(6 eps_0); (2) At face centre -> imagine 2nd cube -> Phi_cube = q/(2 eps_0); (3) At edge midpoint -> 4 cubes -> q/(4 eps_0); (4) At corner -> 8 cubes -> q/(8 eps_0), and flux through each of the 3 faces touching that corner is ZERO!
Disc / Cone solid angle flux: Charge q on axis at distance d from disc of radius R intercepts flux Phi = (q / 2 eps_0) [1 - d / sqrt(R^2 + d^2)] = (q / 2 eps_0)(1 - cos theta).

Symmetric bulk fields: (a) Infinite line lambda: E = lambda / (2 pi eps_0 r); (b) Conducting plane sheet sigma: E = sigma / eps_0 (vs sigma / (2 eps_0) for single non-conducting thin sheet!); (c) Solid non-conducting uniform sphere (Q, R): E_in = k Q r / R^3 = rho r / (3 eps_0), E_out = k Q / r^2.
Infinite thick non-conducting slab (thickness 2d, uniform rho, x from midplane): Inside (|x| <= d): E = rho x / eps_0 (linear); Outside (|x| > d): E = rho d / eps_0 (uniform!).

sections.heading: Electrostatic Potential, Equipotentials, Interaction & Self-Energy
sections.summary: Because electrostatic fields are conservative (curl E = 0), scalar potential V(r) simplifies 3D vector problems into algebraic sums via E = -grad V. Distinguishing mutual interaction energy from total assembly self-energy prevents double-counting.
keyPoints: Field-Potential calculus: dV = -E . dr => E_x = -dV/dx, E_y = -dV/dy, E_z = -dV/dz (field always points in the direction of STEEPEST POTENTIAL DROP!).
Equipotential surfaces: Always perpendicular to field lines; zero work W = q Delta V to move any charge along an equipotential; closer spacing indicates stronger E = -dV/dn.

Potential profiles: Charged ring V = k Q / sqrt(R^2 + x^2); Hollow conducting shell V_in = k Q / R (constant), V_out = k Q / r; Solid non-conducting sphere V_in = k Q (3 R^2 - r^2) / (2 R^3), V_centre = 1.5 V_surface.

Self-energy of isolated spheres: Uniform hollow shell U_self = k Q^2 / (2 R); Uniform solid insulating sphere U_self = 3 k Q^2 / (5 R) (also equals electrostatic field energy integral (1/2) eps_0 E^2 dV over all space!).
Interaction energy of concentric shells (r1, q1 and r2, q2): U_total = k q1^2/(2 r1) + k q2^2/(2 r2) + k q1 q2 / r2 (note interaction term uses OUTER radius r2!).

sections.heading: Conductors, Electrostatic Shielding, Concentric Shells & Earthing
sections.summary: Mobile free electrons inside an isolated electrostatic conductor rearrange instantaneously until bulk internal E = 0 and the entire conductor forms a single equipotential body. Grounding any shell pins its potential to V = 0, forcing charge redistribution and unique induction.
keyPoints: Core conductor properties in electrostatic equilibrium: (1) E_bulk = 0; (2) Excess charge resides strictly on outer surface (and inner cavity walls ONLY if a charge is enclosed inside the cavity!); (3) Surface field just outside = (sigma / eps_0) n_hat perpendicular to surface.
Electrostatic pressure on charged conductor: Outward normal force per unit area P_elec = sigma^2 / (2 eps_0) = (1/2) eps_0 E^2 (factor 1/2 arises because self-layer does not push itself!).

Concentric shells & charge distribution: If charge +q sits inside an uncharged hollow conducting shell, -q induces on inner wall (Gauss surface inside metal has E = 0!) and +q appears uniformly on outer wall, completely shielding exterior from interior position!

Earthing / Grounding rule: Grounded conductor fixes V_conductor = 0 (NOT q_conductor = 0!). Write algebraic sum of potentials from ALL concentric shell charges at the grounded shell and set equal to zero to solve its induced charge.

Connecting two separated conductors (r1, r2) via thin wire: Charge flows until potentials match (k q1'/r1 = k q2'/r2) => final charges split proportional to radii (q1'/q2' = r1/r2), while surface charge densities scale INVERSELY (sigma1'/sigma2' = r2/r1 -> sharper points have higher sigma!).

sections.heading: Capacitors, Dielectric Slabs, Energy Loss & DC RC Transients
sections.summary: Capacitors store electrostatic energy (1/2) C V^2 = Q^2/(2C) inside the electric field between opposing conductors. Inserting dielectrics alters capacitance while battery connection state decides whether Q or V stays invariant; RC loops govern exponential charging and discharging.
keyPoints: Standard capacitances: Parallel plate C = K eps_0 A / d; Spherical isolated C = 4 pi eps_0 R; Concentric spherical C = 4 pi eps_0 a b / (b - a); Cylindrical C = 2 pi eps_0 L / ln(b / a).

Dielectric insertion rules (full slab K): (1) Battery DISCONNECTED -> Q = Q_0 fixed: C -> K C_0, V -> V_0/K, E -> E_0/K, U -> U_0/K; (2) Battery CONNECTED -> V = V_0 fixed: C -> K C_0, Q -> K Q_0, E -> E_0 (unchanged!), U -> K U_0 (battery supplies (K - 1) C_0 V_0^2; half increases U while half is work/heat!).

Split-dielectric combinations: Slabs stacked along gap (same area, thicknesses t1, t2) are in SERIES: C = eps_0 A / (t1/K1 + t2/K2 + d_air). Slabs side-by-side (same gap d, areas A1, A2) are in PARALLEL: C = (eps_0 / d)(K1 A1 + K2 A2). Conducting metal slab (K -> inf, thickness t): C = eps_0 A / (d - t)!

Charge sharing & spark heat loss: Connecting C1 (at V1) and C2 (at V2) gives V_c = (C1 V1 + C2 V2)/(C1 + C2) (watch +/- polarity!) and ALWAYS dissipates heat Delta H = (1/2) [C1 C2 / (C1 + C2)] (V1 - V2)^2.

DC RC Transients (tau = R_eq C): Charging from 0 -> q(t) = C E (1 - e^(-t/tau)), I(t) = (E/R) e^(-t/tau); Discharging -> q(t) = q_0 e^(-t/tau). Circuit limits: at t = 0+ uncharged capacitor acts as SHORT WIRE (V_C = 0); at t -> inf steady state any capacitor acts as OPEN SWITCH (I_C = 0)! Compute R_eq across capacitor terminals after shorting all ideal DC batteries!

derivationsAndGraphs.title: Non-Conducting Solid Sphere vs Conducting Shell E(r) and V(r) Curves
derivationsAndGraphs.expressionOrCurve: Insulating Solid: E_in = kQr/R^3 [linear] ; Conducting Shell: E_in = 0, E_surf = kQ/R^2 [jump], V_in = kQ/R [flat]
derivationsAndGraphs.keyTakeaway: In a hollow metal shell, internal E is strictly zero while internal V stays flat at kQ/R; in a uniform insulating sphere, V peaks at centre at 1.5 x V_surface.

derivationsAndGraphs.title: Uniform Ring Axial Field E(x) & Maximum Point
derivationsAndGraphs.expressionOrCurve: E(x) = k Q x / (R^2 + x^2)^(3/2)  =>  dE/dx = 0 at x = +/- R / sqrt(2) with E_max = 2 k Q / (3 sqrt(3) R^2)
derivationsAndGraphs.keyTakeaway: Changes sign across x = 0; for small x << R, E ~ (kQ/R^3) x, making an opposite charge -q oscillate with SHM!

derivationsAndGraphs.title: RC Charging & Discharging Exponential Curves
derivationsAndGraphs.expressionOrCurve: q(t) = C E (1 - e^(-t / tau)) ; I(t) = (E / R_eq) e^(-t / tau)  where tau = R_eq * C
derivationsAndGraphs.keyTakeaway: At t = tau, capacitor reaches 63.2% of full charge while current drops to 36.8% of initial surge; half of total battery work (1/2)CE^2 is always dissipated as Joule heat in R!

derivationsAndGraphs.title: Plate Force & Energy Density Profile Inside Capacitor
derivationsAndGraphs.expressionOrCurve: F_plate = Q^2 / (2 eps_0 A) = (1/2) C V^2 / d ; u = (1/2) K eps_0 E^2
derivationsAndGraphs.keyTakeaway: Mutual attraction force between plates does NOT equal Q E_total (= Q^2/(eps_0 A)) — it is HALF that because each plate sits only in the other plate's field sigma/(2 eps_0)!

formulas.formula: E_ring = kQx/(R^2+x^2)^(3/2) ; E_disc = (sigma / 2 eps_0)[1 - x / sqrt(R^2+x^2)]
formulas.note: Ring peaks at x = R/sqrt(2); infinite non-conducting sheet -> sigma / (2 eps_0)

formulas.formula: V = k p cos(theta) / r^2 ; E = (k p / r^3) sqrt(1 + 3 cos^2 theta)
formulas.note: Axial (theta=0): 2kp/r^3; Equatorial (theta=90): kp/r^3 anti-parallel to p

formulas.formula: tau = p x E ; U = -p . E ; T = 2 pi sqrt(I / (p E))
formulas.note: Work to rotate from theta1 to theta2 = pE(cos theta1 - cos theta2)

formulas.formula: Phi_cube(corner) = q / (8 eps_0) ; Phi_disc = (q / 2 eps_0)(1 - cos theta)
formulas.note: 3 faces touching corner carry zero flux; face centre -> q / (2 eps_0)

formulas.formula: U_hollow = k Q^2 / (2 R) ; U_solid = 3 k Q^2 / (5 R)
formulas.note: Electrostatic field energy density u = (1/2) K eps_0 E^2

formulas.formula: E_surf = sigma / eps_0 ; P_elec = sigma^2 / (2 eps_0)
formulas.note: Mutual force between capacitor plates = Q^2 / (2 K eps_0 A)

formulas.formula: C = eps_0 A / (d - t + t/K) ; Metal (K -> inf): C = eps_0 A / (d - t)
formulas.note: Series slabs add t_i/K_i in denominator; parallel slabs add K_i A_i in numerator
Watch plate polarity (+/- V2) when connecting opposite plates!

formulas.formula: tau = R_eq * C ; W_battery = C E^2 ; U_stored = (1/2) C E^2 = Heat
formulas.note: Find R_eq across C terminals with all ideal batteries shorted

formulas.formula: q1 / q2 = r1 / r2 ; sigma1 / sigma2 = r2 / r1
formulas.note: Smaller radius sphere holds higher surface charge density sigma

traps: Non-conducting sheet vs Conducting plate: Infinite thin non-conducting sheet has E = sigma / (2 eps_0), whereas a thick conducting plate in vacuum has E = sigma / eps_0 (twice as big!).
Earthing a shell does NOT make its charge zero — it sets its POTENTIAL V = 0! External charges always induce non-zero charge on a grounded conductor.
Dipole in uniform E: Net force is zero ONLY in uniform E; in non-uniform E, F = p (dE/dr) pulls dipole toward higher field if aligned with E.
Dielectric split orientation trap: Splitting gap thickness d -> SERIES (add t_i / K_i in denominator); splitting plate area A -> PARALLEL (add K_i A_i in numerator)!
Capacitor heat dissipation trap: Charging an empty capacitor C from battery V ALWAYS wastes 50% of battery work [(1/2) C V^2] as heat in wires/R regardless of how small R is!
Charging RC time constant error: Do NOT blindly use R_series; short all ideal batteries and find Thevenin R_eq seen across the capacitor leads!

Verify RC circuit currents at t = 0+ (capacitor shorted) and t -> infinity (capacitor open), plus R_eq calculation.

solvedExamples.question: A charge q is placed at one corner of a cube of side a. Find the total electric flux passing through the cube and the flux through each of the 6 individual faces.
steps: Place 7 more identical cubes around the corner to enclose q symmetrically inside a 2a x 2a x 2a super-cube (8 cubes total).
Total flux leaving the super-cube = q / eps_0 => flux through our single cube = q / (8 eps_0).
For the 3 faces of the cube that TOUCH the corner where q sits, vector r lies strictly inside the face plane (E . dA = 0) => flux through each of those 3 faces = 0.
By symmetry, the remaining total flux q / (8 eps_0) divides equally among the 3 opposite faces => flux per opposite face = q / (24 eps_0).
solvedExamples.answer: Total cube flux = q/(8 eps_0) ; 3 touching faces = 0 ; 3 opposite faces = q/(24 eps_0) each
solvedExamples.pitfall: Dividing q / (8 eps_0) equally by 6 faces (giving q / 48 eps_0) instead of recognizing 3 faces carry zero flux!

solvedExamples.question: Two concentric thin conducting spherical shells of radii R and 2R carry charges +Q (inner) and -2Q (outer). If the outer shell is earthed, find the final charge on the outer shell and the potential of the inner shell.
steps: Inner shell is isolated, so its charge remains q_1 = +Q. Let final charge on earthed outer shell be q_2.
Outer shell potential V_2 = 0 (grounded): V_2 = k q_1 / (2 R) + k q_2 / (2 R) = 0.
Solve immediately: q_2 = -q_1 = -Q (so net charge +Q flowed from outer shell to Earth!).
Compute potential of inner shell: V_1 = k q_1 / R + k q_2 / (2 R) = k Q / R - k Q / (2 R) = +k Q / (2 R).
solvedExamples.answer: Outer shell charge = -Q ; Inner shell potential = kQ / (2R)
solvedExamples.pitfall: Setting q_2 = 0 upon earthing, or writing V_2 = k q_1 / R + k q_2 / (2R) using wrong radius R for inner shell's contribution at outer surface!

solvedExamples.question: A 4 uF capacitor charged to 100 V is disconnected from the battery and connected in parallel with an uncharged 12 uF capacitor. Find the common potential and total electrostatic energy lost.
steps: Initial charge Q_1 = C_1 V_1 = 4 uF x 100 V = 400 uC; C_2 = 12 uF, V_2 = 0.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Forgetting that energy is NOT conserved during charge sharing between capacitors — the missing 15 mJ turns into spark heat and EM radiation.

solvedExamples.question: In an RC circuit, a 12 V ideal battery (zero internal r) is connected in series with R_1 = 2 Ohm to a parallel junction of R_2 = 4 Ohm and a series branch containing R_3 = 2 Ohm and C = 3 uF (initially uncharged). Switch closes at t = 0. Find current through the battery at t = 0+ and at t -> infinity, plus the RC time constant tau.
steps: At t = 0+ (uncharged C acts as short wire): R_3 (2 Ohm) is in parallel with R_2 (4 Ohm) => R_par = (2 x 4)/(2 + 4) = 4/3 Ohm.
Total R at t = 0+ is R_1 + R_par = 2 + 4/3 = 10/3 Ohm => battery current I(0+) = 12 / (10/3) = 3.6 A.

At t -> infinity (fully charged C blocks current in R_3-C branch -> open circuit): Current flows ONLY through R_1 + R_2 = 2 + 4 = 6 Ohm => I(inf) = 12 / 6 = 2.0 A (and V_C = V across R_2 = 2 x 4 = 8 V!).
For time constant tau = R_eq * C: Short the 12 V battery, look across C terminals -> R_3 (2 Ohm) is in series with [R_1 || R_2 = (2 x 4)/(2 + 4) = 4/3 Ohm].
Hence R_eq = 2 + 4/3 = 10/3 Ohm => tau = (10/3) x 3 uF = 10 microseconds!
solvedExamples.pitfall: Using R_1 + R_2 + R_3 = 8 Ohm for tau instead of computing R_eq across capacitor leads with battery shorted!

sections.heading: Microscopic Conduction, Drift Velocity & Wire Stretching Laws
sections.summary: An electric field accelerates free electrons between random lattice collisions, establishing steady average drift velocity v_d proportional to E. Resistance depends on both intrinsic temperature-sensitive resistivity rho and conductor geometry, scaling quadratically upon volume-conserving drawing.
keyPoints: Microscopic Ohm's Law: I = n e A v_d, where v_d = (e E / m) tau ~ 10^(-4) m/s (whereas thermal speed ~ 10^5 m/s and EM signal propagates at ~c!). Mobility mu = v_d / E = e tau / m.
Vector conductivity relation: J = I / A = sigma E = n e v_d, giving resistivity rho = 1 / sigma = m / (n e^2 tau) (purely material & temperature property, independent of L or A!).

Temperature dependence rho(T) = rho_0 [1 + alpha (T - T_0)]: Metals have POSITIVE alpha (tau drops with T due to phonon scattering); Semiconductors & Electrolytes have NEGATIVE alpha (carrier density n rises exponentially with T!); Alloys (Manganin, Constantan) have near-zero alpha!

Volume-conserving wire stretching (L -> n L => A -> A / n): R = rho L / A = rho L^2 / V = rho V / A^2 => R proportional to L^2 proportional to 1/A^2 proportional to 1/r^4! Stretching by factor n multiplies R by n^2.
Non-uniform / radial resistance integration: Integrate elemental resistances in series (cylindrical cone dR = rho dx / (pi r(x)^2)) or parallel (hollow spherical shell dR = rho dr / (4 pi r^2)).

sections.heading: Kirchhoff's Laws (KCL/KVL), Cell Combinations & Maximum Power Transfer
sections.summary: Kirchhoff's Current Law enforces charge conservation at nodes while Voltage Law enforces energy conservation around closed loops. Grouping non-ideal cells and matching load resistance to source internal resistance optimize current and power delivery.
keyPoints: KCL & KVL: At any node, Sum(I_in) = Sum(I_out). Around any closed loop, Sum(Delta V) = 0: drop -IR going along assumed current, +IR against it; battery - to + gives +E, + to - gives -E.

Terminal Voltage of Cell (EMF E, internal r): Discharging (current exits + terminal): V = E - I r (< E). Charging (current forced INTO + terminal): V = E + I r (> E). Short-circuited cell: V = 0, I_max = E / r.

Series cells (n cells, opposing polarity count m): E_eq = (n - 2 m) E, r_eq = n r. Parallel cells (E1, r1 and E2, r2): E_eq / r_eq = E1 / r1 +/- E2 / r2 and 1 / r_eq = 1 / r1 + 1 / r2 (check +/- polarity carefully!).
Mixed grouping (m identical rows of n series cells each): R_load maximizes current when external R = total internal resistance = n r / m -> I_max = E_total / (2 R).

Maximum Power Transfer Theorem: Power in external R is P = I^2 R = E^2 R / (R + r)^2, maximized when R = r giving P_max = E^2 / (4 r). At maximum power transfer, electrical efficiency eta = R / (R + r) = 50% strictly!

sections.heading: Symmetric Resistor Networks, Infinite Ladders & Cube Grids
sections.summary: Exploiting reflectional symmetry, parallel-path folding, and shift invariance collapses daunting multi-node resistor meshes into trivial series-parallel equivalents without writing large KVL matrices.
keyPoints: Mirror / Perpendicular-Bisector Symmetry: Any node lying on the perpendicular bisector plane between terminals A and B shares identical potential V_mid = (V_A + V_B)/2; resistors along that symmetry plane carry ZERO current and can be removed, or central junctions detached!
Input-Output Folding Symmetry: Reflections across the line AB merge equipotential symmetric branches in parallel (halving their resistance!).
12-Resistor Cube (each edge R): Across Body Diagonal = (5/6) R; Across Face Diagonal = (3/4) R; Across Adjacent Edge Corners = (7/12) R.
Infinite Ladder Network: Cut after the first repeating cell and replace the remaining infinite tail by X = R_eq -> solve quadratic X = R_series + (R_parallel || X).

Delta-Star & Unbalanced Wheatstone Bridge shortcut: Convert a delta loop (R_a, R_b, R_c) to an equivalent star (R_1 = R_b R_c / Sum R) or use Nodal KCL / Thevenin equivalence whenever a bridge fails R1/R2 = R3/R4!

sections.heading: Joule Heating, Electrical Power Ratings & Bulb Circuits
sections.summary: Dissipated thermal power scales as I^2 R or V^2 / R depending on whether current or voltage is shared across circuit branches. Appliance ratings (P_rated, V_rated) fix component resistance R = V_rated^2 / P_rated rather than actual power consumed.
keyPoints: Joule power identities: P = V I = I^2 R = V^2 / R (1 kWh = 3.6 x 10^6 J). For fixed V source, P proportional to 1/R; for fixed I (series), P proportional to R.
Rated bulb resistance: R_bulb = V_rated^2 / P_rated. Thus a 25 W - 220 V bulb has 4x HIGHER resistance than a 100 W - 220 V bulb!

Series vs Parallel bulb brightness: Connected in PARALLEL across rated V, the HIGHEST-wattage bulb glows brightest (V^2/R). Connected in SERIES across 220 V (or 440 V!), the LOWEST-wattage bulb (highest R) dissipates MORE power (I^2 R) and fuses first!

RC / Capacitor circuit Joule heating vs steady state: Steady-state energy stored in capacitor = (1/2) C V_C^2; battery work = Q_bat * V_bat; Total heat dissipated in ALL resistors = W_bat - Delta U_cap (plus any initial energy release).

Fuse wire rating rule: Melting current depends solely on wire radius r and material (I^2 R proportional to heat loss per area 2 pi r L => I_max proportional to r^(3/2), completely INDEPENDENT of fuse length L!).

sections.heading: Wheatstone Bridge, Meter Bridge & Galvanometer Conversions
sections.summary: Balanced null-point bridges compare unknown resistances independent of source voltage fluctuations, while precision shunts and series multipliers adapt delicate moving-coil galvanometers into wide-range ammeters and voltmeters.
keyPoints: Balanced Wheatstone Bridge: Zero current through galvanometer (V_B = V_D) iff R1 / R2 = R3 / R4 (or R1 R4 = R2 R3). Unbalanced bridge requires KVL/Delta-Star; bridge sensitivity is highest when all four arms are comparable.

Meter Bridge (100 cm uniform Manganin/Constantan wire): X / R = l / (100 - l). Null point shifts toward the HIGHER resistance end! With left/right end corrections alpha, beta: X / R = (l + alpha) / (100 - l + beta).
Galvanometer (resistance G, full-scale deflection current I_g): Current sensitivity I_s = theta / I; Voltage sensitivity V_s = theta / V = I_s / G.

Ammeter conversion (range I > I_g): Connect TINY shunt S = I_g G / (I - I_g) in PARALLEL with G. Effective ammeter resistance R_A = G S / (G + S) < S (ideal ammeter R_A = 0). Always connected in SERIES in a circuit.

Voltmeter conversion (range V > I_g G): Connect LARGE multiplier R_s = (V / I_g) - G in SERIES with G. Effective voltmeter resistance R_V = G + R_s = V / I_g (ideal voltmeter R_V = infinity). Always connected in PARALLEL across load.

traps: 10% stretch error: Increasing wire length by 10% (L' = 1.1 L) multiplies resistance by (1.1)^2 = 1.21 -> 21% increase (NOT 20% and definitely NOT 10%!).
50% stretch or doubling radius: Never use dR/R = -4 dr/r for finite changes! Doubling radius (r' = 2r) drops resistance to R / 2^4 = R / 16!
Series bulb brightness trap: Connecting a 40 W and 100 W bulb in series across 220 V makes the 40 W bulb glow BRIGHTER because it has 2.5x higher resistance and P = I^2 R!
Cell polarity in parallel: If E1 = 6 V (r1 = 1 Ohm) and E2 = 4 V (r2 = 1 Ohm) have OPPOSITE polarities connected together, E_eq = (6/1 - 4/1)/(1 + 1) = 1 V (NOT 5 V!).
Infinite ladder blunder: Cutting off one section leaves the SAME infinite resistance R_eq — do NOT cut off half a section or forget to include the first series/parallel element!
Charging battery terminal voltage: When a 12 V battery (r = 1 Ohm) is being CHARGED by 2 A, its terminal voltage is 12 + 2(1) = 14 V (> EMF!).

solvedExamples.question: A uniform cylindrical copper wire of resistance 10 Ohm is stretched uniformly until its diameter decreases by 20%. Find its new resistance.
steps: Decreasing diameter by 20% leaves new radius r' = 0.8 r = (4/5) r.
Volume conservation: pi r^2 L = pi r'^2 L' => L' / L = (r / r')^2 = (5/4)^2 = 25/16.
Resistance scales as R proportional to 1 / r^4: R' / R = (r / r')^4 = (5/4)^4 = 625 / 256.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Using linear approximation %R = 4 x 20% = 80% -> 18 Ohm (badly wrong for a 20% change!).

solvedExamples.question: In a Meter Bridge, the null point is found at 40 cm from the left end when an unknown resistor X is in the left gap and R = 12 Ohm is in the right gap. When a 12 Ohm resistor is connected in parallel with R, find the new null point.
steps: With R = 12 Ohm: X = 12 x (2 / 3) = 8 Ohm.
Connecting 12 Ohm in parallel with R = 12 Ohm halves right-gap resistance: R_new = (12 x 12) / (12 + 12) = 6 Ohm.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Shifting the null point toward the smaller resistance instead of away from it (since X > R_new now, l' > 50 cm!).

solvedExamples.question: Two bulbs rated (40 W, 220 V) and (100 W, 220 V) are connected in SERIES across a 220 V DC supply. Which bulb consumes more power, and what total power do they draw?
steps: Compute bulb resistances: R_1 (40 W) = 220^2 / 40 = 1210 Ohm; R_2 (100 W) = 220^2 / 100 = 484 Ohm.
In series, current I is identical through both, so P = I^2 R proportional to R => the 40 W bulb (1210 Ohm) consumes 2.5x MORE power and glows brighter!
Total series resistance R_total = 1210 + 484 = 1694 Ohm.
solvedExamples.answer: 40 W bulb glows brighter ; Total power = 28.57 W
solvedExamples.pitfall: Adding powers 40 + 100 = 140 W (only true in parallel across 220 V!) or claiming 100 W bulb glows brighter.

solvedExamples.question: Find the equivalent resistance between points A and B of an infinite ladder where every horizontal top link has R = 2 Ohm and every vertical rung has R_v = 3 Ohm.
steps: Let R_AB = X be the equivalent resistance of the infinite ladder.
Removing the first cell (one 2 Ohm series top resistor and one 3 Ohm vertical shunt resistor) leaves an identical infinite ladder of resistance X connected in parallel with the 3 Ohm rung!
Write recursion equation: X = 2 + (3 * X) / (3 + X).
Solve quadratic (discard negative root): X = [2 + sqrt(4 + 24)] / 2 = 1 + sqrt(7) ~ 3.65 Ohm.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Putting the 2 Ohm resistor on the bottom rail AND top rail without doubling it to 4 Ohm when both rails have resistors!
