solvedExamples.question: A Carnot freezer maintains an interior temperature of -23 C while rejecting heat into a kitchen at 27 C. If 3000 J of heat leaks into the freezer every minute, find the minimum electric power required to keep it at -23 C.
steps: Convert temperatures to Kelvin: T_C = -23 + 273 = 250 K; T_H = 27 + 273 = 300 K.
Compute refrigerator COP: beta = T_C / (T_H - T_C) = 250 / (300 - 250) = 250 / 50 = 5.
Work required per minute: W = Q_C / beta = 3000 J / 5 = 600 J per minute.
Minimum power required = W / t = 600 J / 60 s = 10 W.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Computing COP = T_H / (T_H - T_C) = 6 (Heat Pump formula!) or using Celsius values.

solvedExamples.question: A police car chases a thief along a straight highway. Police car moves at 30 m/s sounding a 500 Hz siren; thief flees ahead at 20 m/s (both speeds in same direction, v_sound = 330 m/s). Find the frequency heard by the thief.
steps: Direction from Source (police) to Observer (thief) is forward (+x).
Observer (thief) moves AWAY from source (+20 m/s) => numerator uses (v - v_L) = 330 - 20 = 310 m/s.
Source (police) moves TOWARD observer (+30 m/s) => denominator uses (v - v_S) = 330 - 30 = 300 m/s.
Compute observed frequency: f' = 500 x (310 / 300) = 500 x (31 / 30) = 516.67 Hz.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Writing (v + 20)/(v + 30) by flipping numerator and denominator signs! Always check: moving AWAY lowers pitch (use - in numerator); source chasing TOWARD raises pitch (use - in denominator).

solvedExamples.question: 1 kg of water at 27 C (300 K) is mixed in an insulated vessel with 1 kg of water at 127 C (400 K) (specific heat c = 4200 J/(kg.K)). Find the final equilibrium temperature and total entropy change of the universe.
steps: Equal masses & equal c => final equilibrium temperature T_f = (300 + 400) / 2 = 350 K.
Entropy change of cold water: Delta S_1 = m c ln(350 / 300) = m c ln(7 / 6).
Entropy change of hot water: Delta S_2 = m c ln(350 / 400) = m c ln(7 / 8).
Total universe entropy change: Delta S_total = m c ln[(7/6)(7/8)] = 4200 * ln(49 / 48) ~ 4200 * (1/48) ~ +86.6 J/K (> 0, strictly irreversible!).
solvedExamples.answer: T_f = 350 K ; Delta S_universe = 4200 ln(49/48) ~ +86.6 J/K
solvedExamples.pitfall: Claiming Delta S_universe = 0 because the vessel is insulated (Q_net = 0)! Thermal conduction across finite Delta T ALWAYS generates positive entropy!

solvedExamples.question: A source emitting 660 Hz sound moves at u = 10 m/s toward a reflecting wall that is simultaneously moving TOWARD the source at w_wall = 20 m/s (v_sound = 330 m/s, still air). A stationary observer stands at rest between the source and the wall. Find the beat frequency heard by this stationary observer.
steps: Direct wave from source (moving toward stationary observer at 10 m/s): f_direct = 660 x [330 / (330 - 10)] = 660 x (330 / 320) = 680.625 Hz.
Step 1 of echo (wall acts as listener moving toward source at 20 m/s): f_wall = 660 x [(330 + 20) / (330 - 10)] = 660 x (350 / 320) = 721.875 Hz.
Step 2 of echo (wall re-emits f_wall as source moving at 20 m/s toward stationary observer): f_echo = f_wall x [330 / (330 - 20)] = 721.875 x (330 / 310).
Beat frequency heard by stationary observer = |f_echo - f_direct| = 768.45 - 680.625 = 87.82 Hz.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Using f_direct = 660 Hz (true ONLY if observer rides WITH the source!) instead of Doppler-shifting the direct wave too for a ground-stationary observer!

weightageNote: Weightage: 4-5% Exclusive IIT JEE Advanced Electromagnetism & Wave Optics Extensions (Spherical/Cylindrical Cavities, Dielectric Pulling Force, Potentiometer Precision & Thin-Film Interference).
syllabusAlert: IIT ADV_ONLY Module: Potentiometer & Cavity Vector Superposition / Dielectric Energy Forces / Thin-Film Interference Phase Inversion are excluded or minimal in NTA JEE Mains yet are classic IIT JEE Advanced Paper 1/2 scoring zones.

sections.heading: Electrostatic Cavity Superposition (Spherical & Cylindrical)
sections.summary: By linearity of Gauss's Law, a cavity carved inside a uniformly charged sphere or infinite cylinder equals the superposition of an intact positive body plus a negative-density body filling the cavity. Remarkable cancellations produce strictly uniform electric fields everywhere inside the cavity.
keyPoints: Uniformly charged sphere (charge density +rho) with off-centre spherical cavity (offset vector d = r_cavity - r_sphere): Superpose +rho full sphere and -rho cavity sphere -> At any point P inside cavity (r_1 from sphere centre, r_2 from cavity centre, r_1 - r_2 = d): E_P = (rho r_1)/(3 eps_0) - (rho r_2)/(3 eps_0) = (rho d) / (3 eps_0)!

Key properties of spherical cavity field: E_cavity is strictly UNIFORM in both magnitude and direction throughout the entire cavity, completely INDEPENDENT of both main sphere radius R and cavity radius a!

Uniformly charged infinite cylinder (+rho) with off-centre parallel cylindrical cavity (offset vector d perp to axis): By cylindrical Gauss Law E = rho r / (2 eps_0), superposition yields uniform cavity field E_cyl_cav = (rho d) / (2 eps_0)!

Potential & equilibrium inside spherical cavity: Because E_cavity is uniform, equipotentials inside the cavity are parallel planes perpendicular to d, and a point charge +q released inside moves with constant acceleration a = q rho d / (3 m eps_0) until hitting the wall (whereas a charge -q inside a solid sphere WITHOUT cavity executes SHM through centre!).

Potential at cavity centre vs sphere centre: Using exact superposition V(r) = V_full(r) - V_cavity(r) at cavity centre (offset d from sphere centre, cavity radius a): V_cav_ctr = (rho / 6 eps_0)(3 R^2 - d^2) - (rho a^2) / (2 eps_0)!

sections.heading: Magnetostatic Cavity Superposition & Rotating Charged Shells
sections.summary: Ampere's Law linearity mirrors electrostatics inside solid cylindrical conductors carrying uniform current density J. Subtracting a negative current density inside an off-centre cylindrical bore reveals a perfectly uniform transverse magnetic field throughout the hole.
keyPoints: Solid infinite cylinder (uniform current density J along z) with parallel cylindrical hole (offset vector d = r_hole - r_wire): Inside wire without hole, B = (mu_0 / 2)(J x r). Superposing +J and -J gives B_hole = (mu_0 / 2) (J x d)!

Key properties of magnetostatic hole field: B_hole is strictly UNIFORM everywhere inside the cylindrical bore, directed perpendicular to BOTH current J and offset vector d, completely independent of wire or bore radii!
Non-uniform radial current J(r): Apply Ampere's Law directly: 2 pi r B(r) = mu_0 * integral_0^r [J(r') 2 pi r' dr'].

Rotating uniformly charged shell/sphere (charge Q, radius R, angular speed omega): Gyromagnetic ratio M / L = Q / (2 M_mass) holds for BOTH hollow shell (I = 2/3 MR^2 -> M = Q omega R^2 / 3) and solid sphere (I = 2/5 MR^2 -> M = Q omega R^2 / 5)!

Magnetic field at centre of rotating charged disc (surface density sigma, R, omega): Breaking into rings dI = sigma (omega / 2 pi) 2 pi r dr = sigma omega r dr gives B_centre = (1/2) mu_0 sigma omega R!

sections.heading: Dielectric Boundary Forces & Capacitor Virtual Work Methods
sections.summary: When a dielectric slab enters a parallel-plate capacitor, fringing fields at the plate edges pull it inward to lower total energy (at fixed Q) or increase battery-assisted energy (at fixed V). Virtual work differentiates total system energy U(x) with respect to insertion depth x to extract the exact pulling force.
keyPoints: Virtual Work Force Law: At FIXED CHARGE Q (battery disconnected): F_x = -(dU / dx)_Q = +(Q^2 / 2 C^2)(dC / dx). At FIXED VOLTAGE V (battery connected): Battery supplies work dW_bat = V dQ = V^2 dC, so F_x = dW_bat/dx - dU/dx = +(1/2) V^2 (dC / dx) = +(dU / dx)_V!

Important force-sign equality: Regardless of whether battery is connected or disconnected, if V = Q / C at a given instant, the instantaneous dielectric pulling force has the EXACT SAME formula F = +(1/2) V^2 (dC / dx) pulling the slab INWARD!

Slab of width b, thickness d, length L partially inserted distance x into capacitor (plates L x b, gap d): Parallel split C(x) = (eps_0 b / d) [K x + (L - x)] => dC/dx = eps_0 b (K - 1) / d => At fixed V: constant inward force F = eps_0 b (K - 1) V^2 / (2 d)!

Liquid dielectric capillary rise between vertical charged plates (gap d, constant V, density rho): Equating upward electrical pull eps_0 b (K - 1) V^2 / (2 d) to weight of risen column (b d h) rho g yields h = eps_0 (K - 1) V^2 / (2 rho g d^2)!

Conducting metal slab partially inserted (fixed V): Equivalent to K -> infinity in capacitance C(x) = eps_0 b [x/(d - t) + (L - x)/d], pulling the metal slab inward with force F = (1/2) eps_0 b t V^2 / [d (d - t)]!

sections.heading: Potentiometer Precision Circuits, Sensitivity & Internal Resistance
sections.summary: Unlike a moving-coil voltmeter that draws load current, a Potentiometer achieves null balance against a calibrated wire potential gradient, acting as an ideal infinite-resistance voltmeter. Balancing open-circuit and shunted cells measures true EMF and tiny internal resistances directly.
keyPoints: Working principle: Driver battery (E_0, r_0) drives steady current I_p = E_0 / (R_wire + R_rh + r_0) through uniform wire of length L and resistance R_wire. Potential gradient k = V_wire / L = I_p R_wire / L (V/m).

Null balance condition: Unknown cell EMF E balances at length l iff E = k * l (zero current in secondary galvanometer branch!). Note: Driver V_wire MUST exceed E (otherwise null point is impossible to find on the wire!).

Applications: (1) Compare two EMFs: E_1 / E_2 = l_1 / l_2; Sum-Difference method: (E_1 + E_2)/(E_1 - E_2) = l_1 / l_2 => E_1/E_2 = (l_1 + l_2)/(l_1 - l_2). (2) Internal resistance r of cell: Open-circuit null l_1 (E = k l_1), shunted by known R null l_2 (V = I R = k l_2) => r = R * (l_1 - l_2) / l_2!
Sensitivity maximization: Lowering potential gradient k (by increasing wire length L or increasing primary series rheostat R_rh) spreads out null lengths and increases precision!

Secondary resistor invariance trap: Any resistor placed IN SERIES inside the secondary galvanometer/test-cell loop causes ZERO shift in null length l (since I_sec = 0 at null!), though it reduces deflection sharpness away from null.

sections.heading: Thin-Film Interference, Lloyd's Mirror & Fresnel Biprism
sections.summary: Reflections from the top and bottom faces of a thin dielectric film interfere with optical path difference 2 n t cos(r) plus any boundary phase jumps. Checking whether zero, one, or both reflections undergo a pi phase inversion determines whether bright fringes satisfy half-integer or integer wavelength conditions.
keyPoints: Boundary reflection phase rule: Reflection off an optically DENSER medium (n_2 > n_1) undergoes a pi phase shift (= lambda / 2 optical path jump). Reflection off a RARER medium (n_2 < n_1) undergoes ZERO phase shift!
Thin film (index mu, thickness t, refracted angle r inside film): Geometrical optical path difference between top and bottom reflected rays = 2 mu t cos(r).

Case A — Soap film in air (Air 1.0 / Film mu / Air 1.0) or Oil on Water (Air 1.0 / Oil 1.4 / Water 1.33): Here ONLY the top reflection inverts phase (pi), so Reflected Constructive (Bright): 2 mu t cos(r) = (2n - 1) lambda / 2; Reflected Destructive (Dark): 2 mu t cos(r) = n lambda (t -> 0 appears BLACK in reflected light!).

Case B — Oil (1.3) on Glass (1.5) in Air (1): BOTH Air->Oil and Oil->Glass are rarer->denser (TWO inversions = 2 pi = 0 net jump!) -> Reflected Bright: 2 mu t cos(r) = n lambda; Reflected Dark: 2 mu t cos(r) = (2n - 1) lambda / 2! (Transmitted light is ALWAYS complementary to reflected light by energy conservation!).

Lloyd's Mirror & Fresnel Biprism: Lloyd's mirror interferes direct ray with grazing-reflected ray (pi phase jump on mirror!), making the zero-path geometric edge fringe DARK! Fresnel biprism (apex angle alpha, index mu, source distance a, screen D = a + b) creates two virtual coherent slits separated by d = 2 a (mu - 1) alpha with beta = lambda (a + b) / d.

derivationsAndGraphs.expressionOrCurve: E_cav = (rho / 3 eps_0)(r_1 - r_2) = (rho d) / (3 eps_0) ; B_hole = (mu_0 / 2)[J x (r_1 - r_2)] = (mu_0 / 2)(J x d)
derivationsAndGraphs.keyTakeaway: Because r_1 - r_2 = d is the fixed vector between centres, all spatial dependence cancels identically inside the cavity!

derivationsAndGraphs.title: Dielectric Slab Force F(x) vs Insertion Depth (Fixed V vs Fixed Q)
derivationsAndGraphs.expressionOrCurve: Fixed V: F(x) = eps_0 b (K-1) V^2 / (2 d) [CONSTANT!] ; Fixed Q: F(x) = Q^2 d (K-1) / [2 eps_0 b (L + (K-1)x)^2] [decays with x]
derivationsAndGraphs.keyTakeaway: At constant battery voltage V, the inward pulling force stays strictly constant throughout insertion; at constant isolated Q, force decreases as slab enters!

derivationsAndGraphs.title: Potentiometer Null Calibration & Shunted Cell Curve
derivationsAndGraphs.expressionOrCurve: E = k l_1 ; V_term = E R / (R + r) = k l_2  =>  r = R (l_1 - l_2) / l_2
derivationsAndGraphs.keyTakeaway: Potentiometer reads true EMF E because zero current flows through internal resistance r at balance.

derivationsAndGraphs.title: Thin-Film Reflected vs Transmitted Complementary Intensity
derivationsAndGraphs.expressionOrCurve: I_reflected + I_transmitted = I_incident  =>  Bright in reflection = Dark in transmission (for single pi-inversion film)
derivationsAndGraphs.keyTakeaway: Very thin soap film (t << lambda) looks completely black in reflected light yet bright in transmitted light!

comparison.title: Thin-Film Reflections, Cavities & Potentiometer Matrix
rows: 2 mu t cos(r) = n lambda (t->0 is BLACK)
2 mu t cos(r) = (2n - 1) lambda/2 (t->0 is BRIGHT)
Independent of sphere R and cavity radius a

traps: Blindly using 2 mu t = (2n - 1) lambda/2 for EVERY thin film! Whenever n_1 < n_2 < n_3 (e.g., anti-reflection MgF_2 n=1.38 coating on glass n=1.5), BOTH boundaries invert phase (net 0 shift), so DESTRUCTIVE reflection needs 2 mu t = (2n - 1) lambda/2!
Potentiometer secondary resistance trap: Placing a 100 Ohm resistor in series with the test cell or galvanometer does NOT shift the null length l (since I = 0 at null!).
Potentiometer no-null condition: If galvanometer deflects to the SAME side at both ends A and B of the wire, either driver polarity opposes test cell OR driver wire voltage < test EMF!
Dielectric force at fixed V vs fixed Q: At fixed V, energy U = (1/2) C V^2 INCREASES as the slab enters, yet the slab is STILL pulled INWARD (because battery supplies +V^2 dC > dU)!
Cavity field radius delusion: Making the spherical cavity 2x wider (at fixed centre-to-centre offset d) does NOT change E_cavity at all!
Fresnel biprism fringe width: Remember total distance D = a + b (from virtual slits at source plane to screen), NOT just b!

solvedExamples.question: A long solid cylindrical conductor of radius R = 5 cm carries uniform current density J = 4 A/cm^2 along +z. A parallel cylindrical hole of radius a = 1 cm is drilled with its axis shifted by d = 3 cm along +x from the wire axis. Find the magnetic field vector inside the hole.
steps: Convert to SI: J = 4 A / (10^(-4) m^2) = 4 x 10^4 A/m^2 along +k; offset d = 0.03 m along +i.
Superpose intact +J cylinder and -J cavity cylinder: B_hole = (mu_0 / 2) (J x d).
Direction: (+k) x (+i) = +j (uniform along +y everywhere inside the bore!).
solvedExamples.pitfall: Including R = 5 cm or a = 1 cm in the cavity field formula, or reversing cross product d x J (-y instead of +y).

solvedExamples.question: A potentiometer wire AB of length 10 m and resistance 20 Ohm is connected in series with a 5 V ideal driver battery and a 30 Ohm rheostat. A test cell gives a null point at l_1 = 600 cm on open circuit, and at l_2 = 500 cm when shunted by R = 10 Ohm. Find the EMF and internal resistance of the test cell.
steps: Total primary loop resistance = R_wire + R_rh = 20 + 30 = 50 Ohm => primary current I_p = 5 / 50 = 0.1 A.
Total voltage across 10 m wire: V_AB = I_p * R_wire = 0.1 x 20 = 2.0 V.
Potential gradient: k = V_AB / L = 2.0 V / 10 m = 0.2 V/m.
Test cell EMF: E = k * l_1 = 0.2 V/m x 6.0 m = 1.20 V.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Computing potential gradient as 5 V / 10 m = 0.5 V/m by ignoring the voltage drop across the 30 Ohm series rheostat!

solvedExamples.question: Find the minimum non-zero thickness of a soap film (n = 1.33) in air that appears bright in reflected light of wavelength 532 nm at normal incidence (cos r = 1).
steps: Check reflection phase shifts: Air (1.0) -> Soap (1.33) gives pi inversion; Soap (1.33) -> Air (1.0) gives 0 inversion.
Net phase difference from reflections = pi (one flip), so reflected constructive interference occurs at 2 n t = (2m - 1) lambda / 2.
For minimum non-zero thickness, take m = 1: 2 n t_min = lambda / 2 => t_min = lambda / (4 n).
Substitute values: t_min = 532 nm / (4 x 1.33) = 532 / 5.32 = 100 nm.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Using 2 n t = lambda (giving t_min = 200 nm) by forgetting the pi reflection phase reversal at the front air-soap boundary!

solvedExamples.question: A parallel-plate capacitor with square plates of side L = 10 cm separated by d = 2 mm is connected to a constant V = 1000 V battery. A dielectric slab (K = 5, thickness d, side L) is partially inserted into the gap and held stationary by a horizontal thread. Find the tension in the thread (eps_0 = 8.85 x 10^(-12) F/m).
steps: For insertion depth x along side L, parallel-split capacitance C(x) = (eps_0 L / d) [K x + (L - x)] = (eps_0 L / d) [L + (K - 1) x].
Compute rate of change: dC / dx = eps_0 L (K - 1) / d.
At constant battery voltage V, inward electrostatic pulling force is F_in = (1/2) V^2 (dC / dx) = eps_0 L (K - 1) V^2 / (2 d).
To hold slab stationary, outward thread tension T = F_in.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Putting a minus sign on -(dU/dx)_V and concluding the capacitor repels the slab outward! At fixed V, F = +(dU/dx)_V pulls INWARD.
